item.title: Dortmund "definitely" want to recruit a central defender in winter
item.description: Dortmund "definitely" want to recruit a central defender in winter Having made a strong start to the Bundesliga season, Borussia Dortmund may be set to bolster their squad depth in winter. As BVB chief journalist Jörg Weiler reports in the BILD podcast 'Dortmund Insider', the central defender position is to be improved. “From what I've heard, they definitely want to bring in another central defender, possibly even from the second division,” Weiler hinted. Weiler didn't list any names, but the fact is, however, that Dortmund has financial leeway in the winter transfer window. A talented defender like Hertha BSC's Linus Gechter (22) could be an option, who was linked with BVB back in October 2025. The bosses of the Westphalian outfit haven't set a fixed budget on their spending, but there is an internal agreement for recruitment. "If someone finds a player that everyone in charge [at Dortmund] is convinced of and can help BVB in the short term (…). "Then they [BVB are] certainly willing to open the coffers in the winter," says Weiler's colleague Maximilian Wessing.

item.title: Bernardo Silva opens up about his situation at Real Madrid – “I want to be useful”
item.description: Bernardo Silva opens up about his situation at Real Madrid – “I want to be useful” This international break will see Bernardo Silva taking on an elevated role for the Portuguese national team. Following Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement, Silva has been appointed as the captain of the pack and he will play a key role in steering the team forward in the coming years. Speaking ahead of Portugal’s UEFA Nations League encounter against Denmark, Silva offered his perspective on his story so far at Real Madrid. Silva wants to feel useful Silva has adopted a deeper midfield role at Real Madrid. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) It is no secret that Silva has had a relatively slow start to life at Real Madrid, notably struggling for game-time in the initial phases. The former Man City star acknowledged that the Real Madrid team is stacked right now, but added he wants to feel useful in the team and that not playing enough always hurts. “It’s always difficult. We all want to play, we all want to be useful. In my career, I have always been used to being useful, to participating. When I don’t participate, it’s obviously tough. “The coach has 27 players, which are many, and only 11 can play at a time. It’s a pretty difficult job, to choose between such a talented team,” he said (h/t Diario AS ). Silva has made only seven starts in La Liga for Real Madrid this season, though he has been more prominent in Jose Mourinho’s plans in recent weeks. “What I can guarantee from me is that I will always give my best and I will always be willing to try to improve and help the team in whatever is necessary, whether it is 5, 10, 30 or 90 minutes. Of course, I want to participate and feel useful,” he added. Silva on playing further back Silva is now the capain of the Portugal team. (Photo by Leonardo Fernandez/Getty Images) Silva made his name in the game by being an illustrious playmaker who can offer creative spark going forward. At Real Madrid, he has adopted a deeper role, often appearing as the deep-lying playmaker. Talking about his position, Silva said, “Now I don’t know exactly why, but I’m more conservative, more thoughtful, very different than I was 10 years ago. That has led me to other positions, a little further back in the midfield. “But I am always available to try to help the National Team and my club in what the coach deems necessary. The coach will have to answer that question. I think he sees me as an 8, a 10, a link between defense and attack. And not as much as an extreme,” he added. Finally, Silva added what coaches now expect from him, now that he is no longer the dynamic playmaker he once was. “ Therefore, that balance between defense and attack, which makes transitions, which helps with the pressure. The player who does a little bit of everything is what the coach expects of me, ” he concluded.

item.title: NFL Academy athlete Luke Francis Jr. looks to ‘put 100%’ into football
item.description: Florida State freshman offensive lineman Luke Francis Jr. , who grew up in Croydon, England, had an unlikely journey to Tallahassee. Francis, a product of the NFL Academy in London, and freshman offensive lineman Nikau Hepi, who came from the NFL Academy’s campus in Australia, are the first NFL Academy athletes to play for the Seminoles. The NFL Academy , established in 2019, is a global initiative run by the NFL to create educational and athletic opportunities for international talent, with the goal of securing athletic scholarships for its members at American universities and colleges. Now a freshman with the Seminoles, Francis reflected on how he got here, the mentors who helped him along the way, and what it will take for other international athletes to follow his path. The journey to American football Francis, a three-star recruit, began his journey to playing American football with his first passion: basketball. “I used to play basketball, and a basketball coach told me I’m too big to play basketball,” Francis said in an interview with the FSView. “[He said] I don’t have the build for basketball, but I have a build for American football, and so he set me up with the NFL Academy … [We] recorded some drills, sent it to them, went to their combine, and they took me in.” Never miss a beat: Sign up for the FSView Newsletter At the NFL Academy, Francis played defensive line for the London Warriors and tested his skills in the trenches against premier American high school programs, including California’s De La Salle High School at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and IMG Academy in Munich, Germany. Those performances, along with a standout showing at FSU’s Big Man Camp in the summer of 2025, earned him offers from Syracuse University, Georgia State University, and FSU. He then moved to the United States for his senior season at Coral Gables Senior High School, where he switched to offensive lineman. For Francis, committing to the ’Noles became a no-brainer. “Coaching, culture, and standards. Those are the three big things … I valued during my recruiting process,” Francis said. “[Offensive line coach Herb] Hand; I love him to death … He’s genuinely became a second father to me with the way he’s able to teach [me] and how understanding he is.” Mentorship, legacy, and FSU’s culture While Francis is part of the first class of NFL Academy players to join the Garnet and Gold, Florida State has a long-standing legacy of international talent. This includes Australian punter Alex Mastromanno, a 2024 consensus All-American, and English offensive lineman Menelik Watson, the 42nd overall pick in the 2013 NFL draft, among others. Francis, a product of the NFL Academy in London, and freshman offensive lineman Nikau Hepi, who came from the NFL Academy’s campus in Australia, are the first NFL Academy athletes to play for the Seminoles. The journey to American football Francis, a three-star recruit, began his journey to playing American football with his first passion: basketball. “I used to play basketball, and a basketball coach told me I’m too big to play basketball,” Francis said in an interview with the FSView. “[He said] I don’t have the build for basketball, but I have a build for American football, and so he set me up with the NFL Academy … [We] recorded some drills, sent it to them, went to their combine, and they took me in.” Never miss a beat: Sign up for the FSView Newsletter At the NFL Academy, Francis played defensive line for the London Warriors and tested his skills in the trenches against premier American high school programs, including California’s De La Salle High School at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and IMG Academy in Munich, Germany. Those performances, along with a standout showing at FSU’s Big Man Camp in the summer of 2025, earned him offers from Syracuse University, Georgia State University, and FSU. He then moved to the United States for his senior season at Coral Gables Senior High School, where he switched to offensive lineman. For Francis, committing to the ’Noles became a no-brainer. “Coaching, culture, and standards. Those are the three big things … I valued during my recruiting process,” Francis said. “[Offensive line coach Herb] Hand; I love him to death … He’s genuinely became a second father to me with the way he’s able to teach [me] and how understanding he is.” Mentorship, legacy, and FSU’s culture While Francis is part of the first class of NFL Academy players to join the Garnet and Gold, Florida State has a long-standing legacy of international talent. This includes Australian punter Alex Mastromanno, a 2024 consensus All-American, and English offensive lineman Menelik Watson, the 42nd overall pick in the 2013 NFL draft, among others. Francis looks forward to learning from these alumni and contributing to that legacy. “It’s an honor … to be able to walk in the footsteps of greats that have come before us like Menelik Watson,” Francis said. “When I first committed [to FSU, Watson] instantly texted me … He became a mentor. [He] wanted to know how he could teach me … he taught me ways to manage myself around the coaches… Having that international community is something that I wouldn’t trade for anything.” Never miss a beat: Sign up for the FSView Newsletter Since signing with the Seminoles on Dec. 3, 2025, and arriving in Tallahassee on Jan. 7, Francis has embraced what it means to play for FSU. “It’s electrifying. It’s addicting. It’s amazing,” Francis said. “You couldn’t ask for a better culture … for better families … for a better tradition … It's an honor to wear the Seminole on my chest every time I run out of that tunnel … It’s an honor to walk around campus with the Seminole on my chest … [and] to go home … and teach people about the great things that FSU has done for me and can do for many others.” Francis is driven by his purpose Francis does not take that duty lightly. That’s why, when he faces adversity, he remembers his “why.” “I just say to myself, ‘What would my mom tell me? What about my brother, my sister, my dad?,’” Francis said. “How would I feel when I get to the point where I can give back to them for how much they put into me?” Francis’ dream of playing American football became a reality because of his commitment to his craft. He said international athletes who want to chase the same dream need to be all in, just like him. “This isn’t something that you don’t take seriously. This is your life,” Francis said. “If this is really something that you want to do, put 100% into it because the second that you put 99% into it, it gets exposed really fast … Learn to love the game … and to be coachable, and this could be something that changes your life forever.” Hunter Milligan is a Senior Staff Writer for the FSView & Florida Flambeau, the student-run, independent online news service for the FSU community. Email our staff at contact@fsview.com . This article originally appeared on FSU News: NFL Academy athlete Luke Francis Jr. looks to ‘put 100%’ into football

item.title: UC Bearcats at Iowa State Cyclones live updates, score, highlights
item.description: AMES, IA – It's brunch with the Bearcats as the University of Cincinnati kicks off at Jack Trice Stadium at 11 a.m. locally, noon in Cincinnati. Post bacon-and-eggs, UC hopes to pancake some Iowa State defenders at Jack Trice Stadium for that elusive sixth win and bowl eligibility. It would also be their first win in November since winning their first Big 12 game in Houston three years ago. They haven't won a road game since defeating Oklahoma State Oct. 18 of last season. After last week's one-score defeat at No. 17 Houston , UC is 1-12 in the 11th month of the year. The Bearcats are 5-4 (2-4 Big 12), with Iowa State's Cyclones coming in 4-5 (2-4 Big 12). Last season, UC defeated No. 14/No. 12 Iowa State at Nippert Stadium 38-30 in their best win of the season. The Cyclones have 83 new players, including Arkansas State transfer quarterback Jaylen Raynor, another dual-threat weapon. Former walk-on Aiden Flora has terrorized defenses with 1,119 rushing yards. Flora has been over 100 yards four times and had 212 yards in shootout wins vs. West Virginia and 221 vs. then-No. 24 Oklahoma State. Arizona, Utah, BYU and Iowa have been the only teams to keep Flora below the century mark. The Bearcats should have running back Cole Tabb back, who left the Houston game in the third quarter with a head injury . Tabb has 812 rushing yards and 14 total touchdowns to lead the Bearcats. UC should also have center Taran Tyo back on the offensive line, but will be without receiver JV Gibson, who left TDECU Stadium in Houston on a stretcher after sustaining a targeting hit in the end zone. Game 🔟 combo #GoBearcats | @jeffwylerauto https://t.co/WCm7GiA4c1 — Cincinnati Football (@GoBearcatsFB) November 12, 2026 Stream Cincinnati Bearcats at Iowa State New updates will appear below, with the most recent at the top. UC Bearcats punter Max Fletcher is Ray Guy Award semifinalist 09:02 AM ET, November 14 2026, Scott Springer Fletcher is one of 10 semifinalists for the 2026 Ray Guy Award. Fletcher has averaged 45.10 gross/43.43 net yards and has pinned opponents inside the 20-yard line 13 times. His career average is 45.3 yards per kick, second to former Cincinnati Bengal and UC James P. Kelly Athletic Hall of Famer Kevin Huber, who averaged 45.47. This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: UC Bearcats at Iowa State Cyclones live updates, score, highlights Our editors independently choose our recommendations. item.title: Arsenal international provides fantastic assist in Ecuador win
item.description: Arsenal international provides fantastic assist in Ecuador win Piero Hincapie provided an assist in Ecuador’s win over Costa Rica overnight, as well as helping the team to keep a clean sheet. Photo by Franklin Jacome/Getty Images Arsenal defender Piero Hincapie made a start for Ecuador against Costa Rica on Friday night, or the early hours of Saturday morning in UK time. It was an impactful appearance, as the 24-year-old set up his team’s opening goal with a wonderful assist in the 22nd minute. Receiving the ball on the left-hand side near the halfway line, Hincapie spotted a gap in the opposition defence, and he slid a pass through to Jordy Caicedo . The striker rounded the goalkeeper and scored for 1-0. Photo by Franklin Jacome/Getty Images Hincapie almost repeated the same assist later in the half, with a very similar pass from a similar situation only narrowly failing to find the striker on that occasion. The defender then could have scored a goal of his own, early in the second half, forcing one of the saves of the match with a shot from the edge of the penalty area. At the other end, Hincapie did a good job of helping Ecuador to hold out until the 68th minute, at which point Costa Rica were reduced to 10 men and their hopes of a result began to fade. A Moises Caicedo penalty made sure of the 2-0 win in the latter stages, with Hincapie coming off shortly after that in the 85th minute. Hincapie has had some injury difficulties this season, only starting three matches for Arsenal in all competitions even when he’s been fit. So the Gunners will be glad to see him getting 85 minutes and playing well. Ecuador are in action once more before the international break ends, facing Bolivia on Tuesday night. Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images

item.title: The 143 best holiday gifts in 2026 – obsessively tested by the Guardian US
item.description: Shatterproof wine glasses, Jellycat plushies, ‘yoga paws’ and more gifts handpicked by our experts The best personalized gift ideas Nothing says holiday cheer quite like panic-browsing websites in pursuit of the perfect gift , toggling between 47 open tabs, eyes straining against your screen’s harsh blue light. But finding an item that elicits a squeal of delight from its recipient is one of the best parts of this time of year, when you have a little help. So we’ve curated 143 presents to reclaim holiday shopping as a joyous activity. We recruited seasoned writers and shopping experts to get into the holiday spirit early, vetting gifts across categories such as kitchen, home, tech and more. For months, we cooked, ate, traveled, hiked, ran, showered and slept with test products by our side. And we roped in our mothers, cats, dogs and the kids in our lives to make sure these gifts really work for the people (and pets!) they are meant for. Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Nick Mokey, Lauren Gould, Karen Yuan, Tracy Allison, Emily Farris, Richard Baguley, Jon Chan, Tim Stevens, Maria Ricapito, Adam Doud, Juno DeMelo, Heather Balogh Rochfort and Guardian staff

item.title: Thieves Towed a £350,000 BTCC Audi From ExCeL London, Then FaceTimed Its Team Boss Asking for Cash
item.description: Adam Weaver, team principal of British Touring Car Championship outfit Power Maxed Racing, took a FaceTime call on Thursday night in which someone showed him the team's stolen Audi and asked him to bring cash to get it back. The car, driven by Dexter Patterson, is valued by the team at about £350,000. Weaver described the call to BBC Hereford & Worcester on Friday. He told the caller it was not happening that night, and the caller said he would be in touch in the morning. A second call, Weaver said, told him police had been alerted and the car was on a road still in London. Before the caller rang again, police told Weaver the car had been recovered close to ExCeL London. The Metropolitan Police told the BBC it does not comment on individual car thefts, so the recovery rests on the team's account. No arrests have been reported. Crews working on racing cars in a pit garage. Representative image, not Power Maxed Racing's team. Photo: Scott Foltz / Pexels How the trailer left the compound The team had brought the car to ExCeL for filming and promotional work. It was loaded into a trailer and left in the venue's secure car park overnight, wheel-clamped and backed up against another vehicle so the doors could not be opened, Weaver said. At about 02:30 GMT on Thursday, he was told, three people got into the site, brought in a vehicle and towed the trailer away with the car still inside. ExCeL London said on Thursday evening that it was aware of "an incident in relation to a vehicle theft" and that its security team was working with relevant stakeholders. The statement as reported does not say how the site was entered or how a clamped trailer was moved. Who would pay for it Dr Anthony Gunter, a criminologist at The Open University, told the BBC he believes the thieves wanted the trailer, which can be broken up and sold in parts, and had not realised the car was inside. His view is that a BTCC car has no market because everyone knows what it is. On that reading, the only person who would pay for it was the team. Social media is what Weaver credits for the outcome. Power Maxed's Facebook post thanked everyone who shared the earlier appeal and "made the car and trailer too hot to be handled." We covered the same pressure play in a stolen $500,000 McLaren in Detroit , where the owner asked 1.1 million followers to find it. The car and the team The team's own paperwork is not consistent on the car. Its announcement of Patterson, a 22-year-old Scot, for 2026 refers to a new Audi S3, while the BTCC's team listing gives the car as an Audi A3 Saloon. The BBC's reporting says only "Audi." The listing also puts the team's base at Weston Subedge near Evesham, while the BBC places it in Studley, Warwickshire. The BBC notes the team's former headquarters near Evesham was destroyed in a fire in 2025. BTCC cars are a regular sight at circuits such as Brands Hatch . This one is due at the team's Black Friday event later this month, according to its Facebook post. Weaver

We covered the same pressure play in a stolen $500,000 McLaren in Detroit , where the owner asked 1.1 million followers to find it. The car and the team The team's own paperwork is not consistent on the car. Its announcement of Patterson, a 22-year-old Scot, for 2026 refers to a new Audi S3, while the BTCC's team listing gives the car as an Audi A3 Saloon. The BBC's reporting says only "Audi." The listing also puts the team's base at Weston Subedge near Evesham, while the BBC places it in Studley, Warwickshire. The BBC notes the team's former headquarters near Evesham was destroyed in a fire in 2025. BTCC cars are a regular sight at circuits such as Brands Hatch . This one is due at the team's Black Friday event later this month, according to its Facebook post. Weaver said he spent Thursday night working out whether to risk gathering the money. Would you have paid to get the car back, or hung up and called the police? Sources: BBC Hereford & Worcester interview with Adam Weaver; statements from ExCeL London and the Metropolitan Police as reported by the BBC; Power Maxed Racing Facebook post; Power Maxed Racing driver announcement ; BTCC team listing. ⚡ Read the full article on Backfire News Sign up for the Backfire Newsletter . For the latest news, follow us on Facebook and Instagram .

item.title: This tiny gamepad with dual analog thumbsticks pushes the limits of portable controllers
item.description: As much as I appreciate the ingenious design of the Nintendo Switch's Joy-Con , my family and I can't stand using them as standalone gamepads. So when we travel with the Switch 2 , we always bring at least one full-size gamepad, plus a couple of 8BitDo's Zero 2 controllers for games that don't use analog thumbsticks. I've spent years hunting for an alternative that pairs the size of the Zero 2 with as much of the functionality of a larger controller as I can get, and CRKD's new Atom Plus is nearly exactly that. But if you have larger hands like I do, you may find the gamepad's focus on portability a struggle. CRKD Atom Plus Where to Buy: $29. … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: What the numbers say about a winner in Cowboys vs 49ers
item.description: Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the 4-5 Dallas Cowboys take on the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers. Cowboys key stats from last week Dak Prescott threw for 335 yards, two touchdowns and finished with a passer rating of 114.2 . He finished the game with a four-play, 65-yard game winning touchdown drive in just 29 seconds. CeeDee Lamb led the team with another massive performance through the air. He racked up an astonishing 195 receiving yards and one touchdown, also fumbling once on an odd play. Javonte Williams and Tyler Goodson finished with a combined 32 carries and 178 yards on the ground. Despite these incredible numbers, the Cowboys offense failed to convert yards into points throughout the day. Held back by turnovers and penalties, it took a fantastic one-handed catch from Ryan Flournoy in the waning moments of the game to sneak out of Indianapolis with a win. DAK PRESCOTT LET IT FLY RYAN FLOURNOY ONE-HANDED CATCH (via: @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/FnxrSX3qbx — B/R Gridiron (@brgridiron) November 8, 2026 49ers key stats from last week Brock Purdy and the 49ers finished last week with 232 passing yards, two passing touchdowns, and one interception. Purdy also rushed for 40 yards and converted a touchdown with his legs. Kaelon Black outrushed Christian McCaffrey on seven less rushing attempts, finishing with 70 yards. McCaffrey remains this biggest threat, however, finishing with 87 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns. The 49ers defense limited Las Vegas to just 24 rushing yards on their way to a 38-17 rout of the Silver and Black. They forced three interceptions, including one pick-six. The formula for San Francisco remains the same after all these years – play efficient offense and let the physical defense swing the game. San Francisco just has too many weapons offensively, especially in the backfield, for this defense to shut them down for 60 minutes. It’s extremely unlikely this turns into a defensive fist fight. item.content:encoded: Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the 4-5 Dallas Cowboys take on the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers. Cowboys key stats from last week Dak Prescott threw for 335 yards, two touchdowns and finished with a passer rating of 114.2 . He finished the game with a four-play, 65-yard game winning touchdown drive in just 29 seconds. CeeDee Lamb led the team with another massive performance through the air. He racked up an astonishing 195 receiving yards and one touchdown, also fumbling once on an odd play. Javonte Williams and Tyler Goodson finished with a combined 32 carries and 178 yards on the ground. Despite these incredible numbers, the Cowboys offense failed to convert yards into points throughout the day. Held back by turnovers and penalties, it took a fantastic one-handed catch from Ryan Flournoy in the waning moments of the game to sneak out of Indianapolis with a win. DAK PRESCOTT LET IT FLY RYAN FLOURNOY ONE-HANDED CATCH (via: @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/FnxrSX3qbx — B/R Gridiron (@brgridiron) November 8, 2026 49ers key stats from last week Brock Purdy and the 49ers finished last week with 232 passing yards, two passing touchdowns, and one interception. Purdy also rushed for 40 yards and converted a touchdown with his legs. Kaelon Black outrushed Christian McCaffrey on seven less rushing attempts, finishing with 70 yards. McCaffrey remains this biggest threat, however, finishing with 87 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns. The 49ers defense limited Las Vegas to just 24 rushing yards on their way to a 38-17 rout of the Silver and Black. They forced three interceptions, including one pick-six. The formula for San Francisco remains the same after all these years – play efficient offense and let the physical defense swing the game. Call an aggressively smart game The Cowboys are going to have to put up points. San Francisco just has too many weapons offensively, especially in the backfield, for this defense to shut them down for 60 minutes. It’s extremely unlikely this turns into a defensive fist fight. With that in mind, this should be the proper week to bust out the gutsy calls. 4th and inches at your own 40? Sounds like a QB sneak to me. Dallas can choose to kick a 57-yard field goal or they can go for it on 4th and 2. This is one time where it’s ok to skip leg day. Send out the offense and attack. Brian Schottenheimer needs to understand what’s at stake here. Nobody expects the Cowboys to win, but a win has the potential to turn this entire season into something meaningful. Call this game like your back is against the wall and your football life is on the line. It’s going to take a gutsy performance from every player and every coach this week if the Cowboys are to stand a chance. What do the numbers mean? The Cowboys are one of the worst rushing defenses in the NFL. The 49ers possess one of the best rushing attacks, utilizing two backs and a scheme where you never know where the ball is going to go. Dallas is also one of the league’s worst third-down defenses while the 49ers convert at a higher rate than almost every team. The 49ers are clearly the better team, especially when looking at their offense against the Cowboys defense. Yet the FanDuel line is only a 4.5 point spread . This tells me that the line setters understand that Dallas has the talent in the building to keep up and win a game against the 49ers. It just takes one week for everything to come together and see an explosion from this Cowboys team. We’ve yet to see it in 2026, however. If Dallas is to stand a chance this week, they’ll need to finally put together a complete performance for the first time this season. They’ll need to play mistake-free football while making the plays on both sides of the ball that they just haven’t done often enough in 2026. And don’t sleep on the special teams performance playing an important role in the field position battle. If the Cowboys put out their best performance on 2026 by playing mistake free football, scoring touchdowns instead of field goals, and winning the turnover differential, I give them a 40-50% chance at winning this game. But from everything we’ve seen, the Cowboys do not play mistake free football. They are unable to consistently get stops on defense, especially against good teams with good rushing attacks. This team has also played several games where the offense has struggled to put points on the board. To top it off, the head coach has made far too many questionable decisions that have directly impacted the results of these games. The Cowboys are the ultimate wild card this week. Put it all together and have a chance to steal a tough win. Play the same brand of football we’ve seen far too often this season, and this could be a multiple score loss. This is the game that determines the team they’ll be the rest of the season.

item.title: NFL Week 10 expert picks, predictions: Moneyline, against the spread
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers throws a pass during the first half of a game against the Minnesota Vikings of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re somehow already in Week 10 of the NFL season, and it kicked off with a surprisingly thrilling game between the Washington Commanders and New York Giants on Thursday night. But there are plenty more fireworks ahead in a pretty good slate of games this week. Of course, things kick off in Germany with a huge showdown between the Detroit Lions and New England Patriots . But don’t sleep on some big contests in each time window for Sunday. Lions fans will be particularly interested in the 1 p.m. ET showdown between the Minnesota Vikings and Green Bay Packers, but Kansas City Chiefs vs. Atlanta Falcons could be a low-key banger. The late afternoon window features all four NFC West teams—all relevant to the Lions’ playoff chase: Seahawks vs. Raiders, Rams vs. Cardinals, and 49ers vs. Cowboys. The night closes out with a somewhat interesting Steelers vs. Bengals game, if you can stomach all the Aaron Rodgers talk. Unfortunately, the week closes out with a Monday night matchup between two hugely disappointing teams: the 0-8 Chargers and the 4-5 Ravens. Here’s our staff picks for every Week 10 game, along with our season-long records. If you don’t see the picks above, click here to see all of our NFL Week 10 picks . Some of us also picked the games against the spread and the over/under totals. To see those, click the appropriate tab in the widget above. Let’s see your picks!

item.title: TNIAAM Reacts Results: Orange fans still have faith
item.description: SYRACUSE, NY - OCTOBER 31: Syracuse Orange Offensive Lineman Kam Pringle (77) lifts Syracuse Orange Quarterback Steve Angeli (9) up for scoring a touchdown during the first half of the College Football game between the SMU Mustangs and the Syracuse Orange on October 31, 2026, at the JMA Wireless Dome in Syracuse, NY. (Photo by Gregory Fisher/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The 2026 Syracuse Orange football season has been a roller coaster and you wouldn’t blame fans if they kept looking up for the next anvil to drop. However this week we asked if you thought the Orange could win two of the final three games and get to 6-6 and bowl eligibility. A pretty nice number believe that Syracuse can finish the job- maybe that’s a bit of faith in the Orange, or maybe it’s just thinking that NC State and Boston College are in worse shape. If Syracuse can get a win in Raleigh today, then that would push them beyond the FanDuel over/under of 4.5 wins. Can Fran Brown’s team get it done? We’ll find out in a few hours.

item.title: Tyrrell Hatton comments on the state of his golf game after taking the solo lead on day three in Dubai
item.description: Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images Tyrrell Hatton will head into the final round of the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai on Sunday with a one-stroke lead. Hatton posted a third-round 68 to move one shot clear of Frenchman Victor Perez with 18 holes left to play. The Englishman is in fine form right now, following his runner-up finish in Abu Dhabi last week. Now Tyrrell Hatton will be hoping to close out his 2026 season in style with a win in Dubai on Sunday. Hatton cannot win the Race to Dubai title, but he would dearly love to win the DP World Tour Championship for the first time in his career. However, with Perez just one stroke behind him, and Rory McIlroy and Jon Rahm positioned well for a final-day charge, Hatton’s task on Sunday will be far from simple. Tyrrell Hatton comments on his golf game after taking the solo lead in Dubai The 35-year-old Englishman addressed the media after firing a third-round 68 on Saturday in Dubai, and he was asked to share how he feels about his golf game. “ Yeah, it was a good day. It was tricky, “ Hatton replied. “ The greens were so fast on the back nine. Every putt I had coming in I think from 13, the par 3, just unbelievably fast. Really happy with how I putted today. Had a few like awkward-length par putts early on, and managed to hold them, which was nice. “ Yeah, overall, just happy with how I played. Generally, I think my iron play has been pretty good these last two weeks. Last week I was really happy with my wedges. This week, it’s a little bit harder to get the wedges right to be honest. “ And then the other thing would be just the putter. I did a lot of work with the start line and reading putts and sort of visualising the ball going in. I think that’s shown these two weeks. “ But does Hatton fancy his chances of winning on Sunday in Dubai? “ I know tomorrow is going to be a tough day, “ the Englishman admitted. “ I’ve got enough experience down these last few holes to know that anything can happen. So yeah, I’ll just go out tomorrow and try my best. I know I can play well around here, and that’s what I’ll try to do. “

item.title: Boxing on DAZN This Weekend: Pacheco vs. Fulghum Details & Upcoming DAZN Boxing Schedule
item.description: Curious about what boxing events will air on DAZN this weekend? Get a look at this weekend’s big event and upcoming cards for the unofficial broadcast home of the sweet science. Undefeated super middleweight prospect Diego Pacheco will take on Darius Fulghum. In July, the Los-Angeles bred Pacheco (26-0, 19 KOs) scored a dominant TKO win over Immanuwel Aleem. Fulghum (15-1-1, 13 KOs) has just one win in his last three fights. He is coming off a third-round stoppage win against Yoanki Urrutia in May. How to watch Pacheco vs. Fulghum Pacheco vs. Fulghum goes down on November 14 The event will take place at the Dignity Health Sports Park in Carson, California The card will begin at 8:00 PM EDT Pacheco vs. Fulghum Card Diego Pacheco vs. Darius Fulghum (Super middleweight) Anthony Olascuaga vs. Yuberjen Martinez (For the WBO flyweight title) Charlie Sheehy vs. Gabriel Flores Jr. (Lightweight) David Adeleye vs. Alexander Flores (Heavyweight) Upcoming Boxing Schedule Get a look at the upcoming boxing schedule after this weekend’s card. Kabayel vs. Hysa (Nov 28) WBC heavyweight champion Agit Kabayel makes his first title defense when he meets Nelson Hysa. The German native Kabayel (27-0, 19 KOs) has six consecutive wins via stoppage in his last six outings. He was elevated to full WBC champion in June, after former undisputed heavyweight kingpin Oleksandr Usyk vacated the titles. Hysa (25-0, 23 KOs) brings heavy hands of his own, with only two of his 25 wins going the full distance. How to watch Kabayel vs. Hysa Kabayel vs. Hysa goes down on November 28 The event will take place at the Merkur Spiel-Arena in Düsseldorf, Germany The card will begin at 12:00 PM EDT Kabayel vs. Hysa Card Agit Kabayel vs. Nelson Hysa (For the WBC heavyweight title) Aloys Junior vs. Artur Mann (Cruiserweight) Gleb Bakshi vs. Serhat Parlak (Super middleweight) Benavidez vs. Cieslak (Dec 5) Three-division champion David Benavidez will put the WBA (Super), and WBO titles on the line when he meets WBC titleholder Michal Cieslak in a cruiserweight unification bout. In May, Benavidez (32-0, 26 KOs) made his cruiserweight debut with a huge knockout win over Gilberto Ramirez to claim the championship titles. Cieslak (28-2, 22 KOs) has won nine of his last 10 fights, each of those wins have come via stoppage. How to watch Benavidez vs. Cieslak Benavidez vs. Cieslak goes down on December 5 The event will take place at the Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Arizona The card will begin at 8:00 PM EDT Benavidez vs. Cieslak Card David Benavidez vs. Michal Cieslak (For the WBA, WBO, and WBC cruiserweight titles) Vergil Ortiz vs. Keith Thurman (Middleweight) Emiliano Vargas vs. Omar Juarez (Junior welterweight) Marco Romero vs. Cruse Stewart (Super middleweight) Nikita Tszyu vs. Roberto Valenzuela Jr. (Junior middleweight) Related Headlines Habs Daily: Defensive French Connection, 23 Or 24 Stanley Cups, Leading The NHL, MacKinnon & Makar Michigan Basketball Needs Impactful Minutes from Bench Gl

Arrowhead Stadium notably hosted a 2025 college football matchup between Nebraska and the Cincinnati Bearcats. The game featured rookie Chiefs players Emmett Johnson and Cyrus Allen. Brittany Mahomes Has Priceless Reaction to Wild Chiefs Super Bowl Pregnancy Theory | Sports Illustrated On Nov. 12, Brittany reshared a Complex Sports post that read “EVERY SEASON BRITTANY MAHOMES IS PREGNANT, THE CHIEFS MAKE THE SUPER BOWL” to her Instagram story and added a caption of her own. “Glad someone finally figured this out, just doing my part over here 😂😝😆,” she wrote. Around the NF L Kirk Cousins to start for Vikings vs. Packers on Sunday, five days after trade from Raiders | NFL.com “Cannot give him enough credit for coming in here, how he’s gone about the week, both him and the coaching staff getting him ready to go, using all the time we possibly can,” O’Connell said. “It’s been really impressive what he’s been able to do and just the command and just getting right back in the huddle with a lot of guys he’s played with, but certainly some guys he hasn’t. It’s been something that everybody’s been very, very impressed by.” Cousins’ start will come just five days after he was acquired in a trade with the Las Vegas Raiders. He’ll take the field donning No. 8, which he wore during his initial stint with Minnesota from 2018-2023. Ravens QB Lamar Jackson undergoes thumb surgery, expected to be out 6-10 weeks | Yahoo! Sports Jackson, who had been out since Week 4 with an ankle injury, suffered the injury during his first pass in Week 8, making contact with the hand of Bills linebacker Gregory Rousseau. The quarterback left the game immediately and did not return. He was placed on injured reserve later that week with the hope that he could return later this season. The Ravens have eight games remaining in the regular season and still have their bye week awaiting them in Week 13. A six-to-10 week recovery timeline certainly allows for Jackson, who reportedly told teammates to “just stay alive,” to return this season. But that could also depend on where the team is in the AFC playoff hunt when he’s approaching 100% healthy and ready to play. Fernando Mendoza, Carson Beck, Kyle McCord set to make NFL history with first starts, debuts | CBS Sports This week, we have more to look forward to: Three QBs each get their first starts and make history while doing so. Mendoza is set to make his first start for the Raiders, facing the Seattle Seahawks, and rookie third-rounder Carson Beck will make his NFL debut with the Arizona Cardinals. Another quarterback joining the group of first-timers is 2025 sixth-rounder Kyle McCord, who is making his NFL debut this week as the Miami Dolphins starter. If the three of them do start, 50 quarterbacks will have made at least one start through Week 10 this season, tied for second-most in the past 20 seasons. Only 2019 saw more quarterbacks, when 51 quarterbacks had at least one start through Week 10. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Arrowhead Pride Midseason Awards: The Chiefs’ Special Teams MVP That really only leaves two viable options: Emmett Johnson– who has just started to come on as a kick returner OR punter Matt Araiza, who is statistically among the league leaders at his position this year. Through eight games, Araiza has punted 25 times for 1,270 yards, averaging 50.8 yards per punt. His longest punt of the season is a 69-yard boot, and he’s placed 12 punts inside the 20-yard line. item.title: How much relief will the Spencers provide?
item.description: ATLANTA, GA - SEPTEMBER 30: Atlanta Braves pitcher Spencer Strider (l), Braves pitcher Max Fried (54), Braves pitcher Charlie Morton (50) and Braves pitcher Spencer Schwellenbach (r) celebrate in the locker room after the Braves win the final regular season MLB baseball game of 2024 between the New York Mets and the Atlanta Braves on September 30, 2024 at Truist Park in Atlanta, Georgia. The Braves will go on to San Diego to play the Padres in the Wildcard playoff. (Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images I was one of those fans surprised (yet not surprised) with the Evan Phillips signing. I can squint and see it working out, but it was probably one year and/or $2 MM AAV too much. With one reliever signed, the focus shifts to whether or not Raisel Iglesias returns. There is probably a number there that would make me comfortable with that. But another thought brings me to two pitchers that are recovering from injuries. Spencer Strider and Spencer Schwellenbach could serve anywhere from starters to swingmen to multiple inning guys to high leverage. That is, assuming they can pitch at all in 2027. Having trouble viewing this? Open in a new window . Alex Anthopoulos has already told us that he’s not counting on either to start the year in the rotation. But there is a lot of room between being a starter out of Spring Training and pitching at all. Spencer Strider has a career 3.45/2.83/2.72 in the first time through the order. That will definitely play and will play up in a one to two inning outing. Schwellenbach’s numbers are a juicy 2.04/2.79/2.91, which honestly sounds like a lot of fun in high leverage. Of course, if these guys can’t start, the rotation options after Chris Sale are young Didier Fuentes, the Grant Holmes Experience, Bryce Elder, AJ Smith-Shawver, Joey Wentz, JR Ritchie, and Owen Murphy. This is assuming Tyler Mahle doesn’t return. So how many relief innings will the Braves get from Spencer Strider and Spencer Schwellenbach? Will the Braves put them in a position to pitch fewer than three innings at a time? Will injury force their hand? See, this is why I wasn’t super excited for the offseason this year. Too many questions and too much time.

item.title: Drake Maye and other Patriots links up with Bayern Munich players at Säbener Straße
item.description: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 13: Serge Gnabry of FC Bayern München visits a training session of the NFL Team New England Patriots at Saebener Strasse training ground on November 13, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Sebastian Widmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images When in Munich, why not spend some time with FC Bayern? New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye got a taste of the original brand of football, meeting up with several Bayern Munich players while in town for the NFL’s final International Game of the year. It is not every day that one of the NFL’s young quarterbacks gets to hang out with some of the biggest names in German soccer. But with the NFL bringing its international schedule to Munich, Maye had a great opportunity to make the crossover happen. Bayern and the NFL might play very different games, but they share a city for the occasion—and this meeting made for a fun little collision of sporting worlds. Maye is in Munich as the Patriots take part in the final International Game of the NFL calendar this year. And apparently, his trip has included a little time wi th local soccer royalty, too. Who knows? Maybe a few Bayern players will return the favor and show up at an NFL game sometime soon. The meeting was shared by @iMiaSanMia on X. Join the conversation! item.title: Como sets high asking price for Juventus target
item.description: Como sets high asking price for Juventus target Several players at Como have been performing impressively this season, helping Cesc Fabregas’ side exceed expectations. Their form has attracted interest from major clubs, but Como are determined to keep their most important players as they look to maintain their progress. One of the players attracting attention is Martin Baturina, who has emerged as a transfer target for Juventus. The Bianconeri are interested in bringing the attacking midfielder to Turin after watching him make a strong impression since joining Como. Baturina has been in excellent form and has established himself as an important member of Fabregas’ team. Juventus believe he has the qualities to make a difference in their squad, but securing his signature could prove difficult given his importance to Como. Juventus target Como midfielder The midfielder’s performances have helped Como establish themselves as one of the most impressive sides in the league. His contribution has made him an important player for the club, meaning they have little reason to allow him to leave without receiving a substantial fee. According to TuttoJuve , Como want around €80m for the midfielder, reflecting how highly they rate him and the importance they attach to keeping him in their squad. (Photo by Giuseppe Bellini/Getty Images) Como place huge valuation on Baturina An €80m asking price would make any potential move a major investment for Juventus. Although the Bianconeri are a much bigger club and could appeal to the 23-year-old, Como’s valuation means they would need to make a significant financial commitment. Baturina could be attracted by the opportunity to join Juventus and take the next step in his career. However, the size of the proposed fee could complicate negotiations, particularly if the Bianconeri are unwilling to spend that much on one player. Como will want to retain a key figure in their squad, while Juventus must decide whether Baturina is worth the asking price. For now, the midfielder’s future remains uncertain, with his performances continuing to attract attention.

item.title: Important Games to Watch: College Football Week 11
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA - OCTOBER 31: Jayden Maiava (14) of the USC Trojans looks to pass during a college football game against the Ohio State Buckeyes on October 31, 2026 at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Joe Robbins/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Playoff hopes are on life support for the Tigers, so if they don’t handle business on Saturday night in Death Valley, none of this will actually matter. The Tigers will need a lot of help going forward, so here are a few games to watch this Saturday. Missouri will be looking to bounce back after losing at home to Texas last week. The Tigers will be traveling to Athens to take on the No. 1 team in the country, Georgia. Georgia is the best team in the country right now, and the Bulldogs are favored to win by nearly 17 points. If Missouri can do the improbable and pull off the victory, it would help elevate LSU a little bit in the rankings. This game will kick off at 2:30 p.m. on ABC. Another important matchup will take place at 11 a.m. on ESPN. Wake Forest goes on the road to play SMU. The Mustangs are currently 1.5-point favorites at home, and if they can hold serve against a surprising Demon Deacons squad, it would give SMU an upset victory over a top-15 team. Finally, USC goes on the road to Bloomington to take on Indiana. The Hoosiers have had several tough matchups lately and are a little banged up. QB Josh Hoover was not listed on the initial injury report, which is a good sign, as he has been dealing with a right shoulder injury. However, RB Turbo Richard will not be playing, and this could be an opportunity for the Trojans to force Indiana to rely heavily on Josh Hoover. This will be the featured game on CBS at 2:30 p.m. on Saturday. What are some of the games you are looking forward to watching this Saturday?

item.title: Steve Smith Sr says he has one big question mark around Kirk Cousins after Vikings return
item.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images Kirk Cousins feels like a much-needed new addition for the Minnesota Vikings but Steve Smith Sr still has one concern. Cousins has previously shone for the Vikings, managing over 4,000 passing yards in four of his previous seasons with the NFL outfit. That return should be especially helpful in 2026 as Minnesota’s current quarterback options have been pretty subpar. However, when speaking to ESPN this week, Smith has expressed concerns about Cousins’ arm strength. He also suggested that the Las Vegas Raiders’ willingness to trade him this season was in part due to his arm strength being an issue. Smith said: “My question mark is: what and how does Kevin O’Connell deal with the lack of arm strength that Kirk Cousins has this go-round? “Yes, because what he was before was a younger Kirk. But you can see, which I believe had something to do with the Las Vegas Raiders allowing him to go to Minnesota, that his lack of arm strength was an issue. “His arm, really. He had some underthrown throws, which led to him now being an opportunity for Minnesota, and it gave the Las Vegas Raiders an opportunity. Based on what I’m hearing, they feel like he’s ready.” Still, even if he is not the player he was back in 2023, he should still be an upgrade on Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz, who have managed fewer passing yards combined than Cousins in 2026. Cousins could make his second debut on Sunday against the Green Bay Packers and it will be interesting to see how much of an impact he has on the Vikings’ offence. Read more: Stephen A. item.title: Who is the next Phillies player to win a major award?
item.description: SURPRISE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 14: Aidan Miller #4 of the Philadelphia Phillies runs to first base on an RBI single during a game between the Peoria Javelinas and Surprise Saguaros at Surprise Stadium on October 14, 2026 in Surprise, Arizona. (Photo by Brandon Sloter/Getty Images) | Getty Images Once again, awards season has come and gone without a Phillies player being named a victor. Cristopher Sanchez was the closest, finishing second in NL Cy Young voting, though even that was close as Chris Sale finished hair’s breadth to him in third. In NL MVP voting, the team had three players on the ballot with Sanchez finishing 8th, Kyle Schwarber finishing 11th and Bryce Harper a distant 15th in voting. The question for today is: who is the next player from the Phillies that will win a major award? When it comes to the big ones of Cy Young and MVP, those feel difficult for the anyone on the team to attain considering the great players that populate the National League right now. My eyes would be looking at the Rookie of the Year award, focusing on Aidan Miller and Francisco Renteria. Those seem like the two players that might actually have a shot at doing something with that award.

item.title: Is Ernie Sims the answer for FSU football's defense? Sure looks like it
item.description: Florida State football's season has been defined by instability, disappointing results and a coaching change. Yet amid the turmoil, one of the most encouraging developments has emerged on the defensive side of the ball, where interim defensive coordinator Ernie Sims has helped spark a unit that suddenly looks more aggressive, confident and connected. Two straight road victories over Boston College and Pittsburgh do not erase the Seminoles' struggles, but they do raise an important question: Has Sims done enough to earn a long-term role in FSU's future? The answer is becoming harder to ignore. REPORT CARD: FSU football grades vs. Pitt: Defense earns high marks on road win A different energy on FSU's defense From the moment Sims took over defensive coordinator duties following Tony White's departure , the defense appeared to take on his personality. The former FSU All-American coaches with the same intensity and edge that defined his playing career. That energy has been evident on the field during the Seminoles' back-to-back wins. FSU has played more physical football, particularly in critical situations. The Seminoles have generated stops on third and fourth down, tackled with greater urgency and shown a willingness to attack rather than react. The level of competition should be acknowledged. Neither Boston College nor Pittsburgh fielded one of the ACC's top offenses. But context matters less than the visible improvement. The defense looks faster, more decisive and more confident than it did earlier in the season. A two-game sample size is not enough to guarantee Sims a promotion, but it is enough to make him a serious candidate for consideration if FSU's next head coach is evaluating the staff from merit rather than reputation. Simplicity has produced results What stands out most about Sims' approach is how uncomplicated it appears. With injuries continuing to deplete the roster, FSU could have easily used personnel shortages as an excuse. Instead, the defense has responded with some of its most disciplined performances of the season. Players have repeatedly pointed to a simpler scheme that allows them to play faster. "I feel like Coach Ernie just changed the defense up," defensive lineman Deamontae Diggs said after the Pittsburgh victory. "(He) let us just play fast and play physical. It's simple, and we just fly around and hit people." The results support that sentiment. item.content:encoded: Florida State football's season has been defined by instability, disappointing results and a coaching change. Yet amid the turmoil, one of the most encouraging developments has emerged on the defensive side of the ball, where interim defensive coordinator Ernie Sims has helped spark a unit that suddenly looks more aggressive, confident and connected. Two straight road victories over Boston College and Pittsburgh do not erase the Seminoles' struggles, but they do raise an important question: Has Sims done enough to earn a long-term role in FSU's future? The answer is becoming harder to ignore. REPORT CARD: FSU football grades vs. Pitt: Defense earns high marks on road win A different energy on FSU's defense From the moment Sims took over defensive coordinator duties following Tony White's departure , the defense appeared to take on his personality. The former FSU All-American coaches with the same intensity and edge that defined his playing career. That energy has been evident on the field during the Seminoles' back-to-back wins. FSU has played more physical football, particularly in critical situations. The Seminoles have generated stops on third and fourth down, tackled with greater urgency and shown a willingness to attack rather than react. The level of competition should be acknowledged. Neither Boston College nor Pittsburgh fielded one of the ACC's top offenses. But context matters less than the visible improvement. The defense looks faster, more decisive and more confident than it did earlier in the season. A two-game sample size is not enough to guarantee Sims a promotion, but it is enough to make him a serious candidate for consideration if FSU's next head coach is evaluating the staff from merit rather than reputation. Simplicity has produced results What stands out most about Sims' approach is how uncomplicated it appears. With injuries continuing to deplete the roster, FSU could have easily used personnel shortages as an excuse. Instead, the defense has responded with some of its most disciplined performances of the season. Players have repeatedly pointed to a simpler scheme that allows them to play faster. "I feel like Coach Ernie just changed the defense up," defensive lineman Deamontae Diggs said after the Pittsburgh victory. "(He) let us just play fast and play physical. It's simple, and we just fly around and hit people." The results support that sentiment. Diggs helped create one of the game's biggest turning points when he tipped a pass from Corey Dailey that led to a Rylan Kennedy interception. The turnover set up FSU's only touchdown of the night. Other players have elevated their play as well. Charles Lester III delivered two key pass breakups and nearly returned an interception for a touchdown. Nehemiah Chandler has been increasingly reliable in coverage while also making open-field tackles. Perhaps most impressive was how the defense responded after Chris Jones was ejected for targeting. Rather than unravel, FSU found answers. Omar Graham Jr. and Caleb LaValle delivered key stops on critical downs to help secure the victory. For a defense that spent much of the season struggling in situational football, those moments represented meaningful progress. More: Ernie Sims' legacy comes home as North Florida Christian retires No. 34 The final two games are Ernie Sims' audition At 5-5, FSU remains one win away from bowl eligibility. Considering where the program stood after Mike Norvell's dismissal, reaching a bowl game would qualify as a significant accomplishment and a stabilizing finish to a turbulent season. The Seminoles' final two games at Doak Campbell Stadium will provide the clearest measure yet of Sims' impact. North Carolina State appears to be the more manageable matchup after the Wolfpack moved on from head coach Dave Doeren. Florida presents a much more difficult challenge, particularly for a defense still battling injuries while attempting to contain one of the SEC's most dynamic rushing attacks led by Jaden Baugh. These games will matter beyond the win-loss record. They will serve as the final evaluation period for a coaching staff operating under interim circumstances while the program prepares for a new era. If the defense continues to perform at its current level, Sims' body of work will become increasingly difficult for the incoming head coach to overlook. Why Ernie Sims should remain at FSU Whether Sims ultimately becomes defensive coordinator is a separate discussion. A new head coach may bring his own staff. If FSU hires a defensive-minded coach, retaining Sims in that role becomes less likely. Those realities are part of modern college football. Still, the broader argument is clear. Sims has demonstrated the ability to connect with players, maximize limited personnel and create tangible improvement in a short period of time. Those are valuable traits regardless of title. Just as important, he represents the culture and identity FSU is trying to preserve through a period of transition. The university recently reinforced that philosophy by hiring FSU alumnus Jeff Purinton as athletics director . Sims fits that same mold as a former Seminole who understands the program's standards and expectations. Even if he is not retained as defensive coordinator, there is a compelling case for keeping him on staff in some capacity. The next head coach will have bigger decisions to make than determining Sims' job title. But after two consecutive road wins and noticeable defensive improvement, keeping Sims in Tallahassee should be among those considerations. The final two games will help shape his future, but the early evidence is encouraging. FSU's defense is playing harder, faster and with renewed confidence under his leadership. That alone does not guarantee a promotion. It does, however, suggest that Sims has earned something equally important: a legitimate place in the conversation about the Seminoles' future. More: Jeff Purinton journey from Florida State SID to new athletic director Florida State 2026 schedule Aug. 29: vs. New Mexico State , W 34-17 Sept. 7: vs. SMU , L, 27-24 Sept. 13: Bye Sept. 19: at Alabama , L 50-36 Sept. 26: vs. Central Arkansas, W 34-7 Oct. 3: vs. Virginia , W 38-7 Oct. 9: at Louisville , L 44-20 Oct. 17: at Miami , L 43-35 2 OT Oct. 24: Bye Oct. 31: vs. Clemson , L 36-24 Nov. 7: at Boston College, W 31-24 Nov. 13: at Pittsburgh , W 16-10 Nov. 21: vs. NC State , 3:30 p.m. Nov. 27: vs. Florida , 3:30 p.m. (ABC, Friday) More: Recap: FSU football holds off Pitt, 16-10, wins second straight road game Peter Holland Jr. covers Florida State athletics and Big Bend Preps for the Tallahassee Democrat. If you'd like to pitch a story on a high school athlete, don't hesitate to get in touch with him via email at PHolland@Gannett.com or on X @_Da_pistol. item.title: ROUNDTABLE: Northwestern football vs. No. 20 Ohio State Buckeyes
item.description: EVANSTON, IL - NOVEMBER 07: Northwestern Wildcats quarterback Nicco Marchiol (4) passes the ball during a college football game between the Iowa Hawkeyes and the Northwestern Wildcats on November 7, 2026, at Ryan Field in Evanston, IL. (Photo by Patrick Gorski/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Northwestern’s season is starting to go off the rails. The ‘Cats are on a two game losing streak and now travel to face Ohio State without its starting quarterback. Nicco Marchiol and company will have to pull off a miracle to get NU back on track. Northwestern (6-3, 3-3 B1G) looks to shock the world and knock off Ohio State (6-3, 4-2 B1G) in a playoff-eliminating matchup in Columbus. Here’s how Inside NU is feeling. Charlie Jacobs (34-23 Ohio State ) Neither Northwestern’s nor Ohio State’s defenses have been playing that well lately. Two weeks ago, Northwestern allowed 34 points to Oregon and followed that up by allowing 24 to Iowa, including 14 in the first half. This past weekend, Ohio State took an early 14-0 lead over Oregon and then gave up 38 unanswered for a total of 41. Going to play in Columbus will certainly test the Wildcat defense, while the Buckeyes will be licking their lips at Nicco Marchiol. I wouldn’t be surprised with either outcome, but right now I’m taking the Buckeyes. Whitley Williams (38-21 Ohio State ) The quarterback is the most important position in football, and both Northwestern and Ohio State will be without their center piece quarterbacks. The No. 20 Buckeyes have dropped back-to-back pivotal games to USC and Oregon, while the ‘Cats have also lost their last two. Defensively, the Wildcats must capitalize on Ohio State’s glaring pass-rush struggles. The Buckeyes have surrendered 71 points over the last two games, and their defensive line has struggled to generate pressure, posting a 3.6% sack rate. On the flip side, the Buckeyes boast arguably the best wide receiver in college football in Jeremiah Smith. Containing him at all costs is a must if the Wildcats hope to keep this game competitive. Northwestern has deviated from its winning formula in recent weeks and the results have shown both in the statistics and on the scoreboard. To get back on track, Caleb Komolafe and Joseph Himon II must be the focal points of the offense, picking up chunk yardage and showcasing their electric speed. Wildcats quarterback Nicco Marchiol appeared unsettled in the pocket against Iowa. With another week of preparation under his belt, Marchiol must demonstrate greater poise and accuracy. Ohio State is overpowered in pretty much every facet on the field. item.content:encoded: EVANSTON, IL - NOVEMBER 07: Northwestern Wildcats quarterback Nicco Marchiol (4) passes the ball during a college football game between the Iowa Hawkeyes and the Northwestern Wildcats on November 7, 2026, at Ryan Field in Evanston, IL. (Photo by Patrick Gorski/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Northwestern’s season is starting to go off the rails. The ‘Cats are on a two game losing streak and now travel to face Ohio State without its starting quarterback. Nicco Marchiol and company will have to pull off a miracle to get NU back on track. Northwestern (6-3, 3-3 B1G) looks to shock the world and knock off Ohio State (6-3, 4-2 B1G) in a playoff-eliminating matchup in Columbus. Here’s how Inside NU is feeling. Charlie Jacobs (34-23 Ohio State ) Neither Northwestern’s nor Ohio State’s defenses have been playing that well lately. Two weeks ago, Northwestern allowed 34 points to Oregon and followed that up by allowing 24 to Iowa, including 14 in the first half. This past weekend, Ohio State took an early 14-0 lead over Oregon and then gave up 38 unanswered for a total of 41. Going to play in Columbus will certainly test the Wildcat defense, while the Buckeyes will be licking their lips at Nicco Marchiol. I wouldn’t be surprised with either outcome, but right now I’m taking the Buckeyes. Whitley Williams (38-21 Ohio State ) The quarterback is the most important position in football, and both Northwestern and Ohio State will be without their center piece quarterbacks. The No. 20 Buckeyes have dropped back-to-back pivotal games to USC and Oregon, while the ‘Cats have also lost their last two. Defensively, the Wildcats must capitalize on Ohio State’s glaring pass-rush struggles. The Buckeyes have surrendered 71 points over the last two games, and their defensive line has struggled to generate pressure, posting a 3.6% sack rate. On the flip side, the Buckeyes boast arguably the best wide receiver in college football in Jeremiah Smith. Containing him at all costs is a must if the Wildcats hope to keep this game competitive. Northwestern has deviated from its winning formula in recent weeks and the results have shown both in the statistics and on the scoreboard. To get back on track, Caleb Komolafe and Joseph Himon II must be the focal points of the offense, picking up chunk yardage and showcasing their electric speed. Wildcats quarterback Nicco Marchiol appeared unsettled in the pocket against Iowa. With another week of preparation under his belt, Marchiol must demonstrate greater poise and accuracy. Winning at the Shoe is no easy feat, and Northwestern will have to be on point to have a chance at pulling off an upset. Zac Penson (28-10 Ohio State ) Without Aidan Chiles, the situation is bleak. Ohio State is overpowered in pretty much every facet on the field. The one advantage Northwestern had was at quarterback which originally would have made this an extremely competitive game, but alas here we are with Nicco Marchiol again. My take from last week was that Marchiol really wasn’t that bad, but the play calling was way too conservative. If the Wildcats want any chance of staying competitive, they have to take risks and move the ball down the field. Last week, Marchiol’s only real strategy was short dump offs to Dehnicke, Wilde and Eligon. Each four or so yard gain would bring up third-and-1, which the ‘Cats would fail to convert and either go for it or boot it away on fourth down. If this strategy didn’t work at home against Iowa, it sure isn’t working at the Shoe against the Buckeyes. The one “benefit” Northwestern has defensively is that starting QB Julian Sayin is out for Ohio State and since his injury they have struggled to move the ball down the field. But even against teams that don’t have Jeremiah Smith as a receiver, Northwestern’s defense has struggled this season. One doesn’t need to look much further than Iowa’s first drive last week to see that. All that being said, I don’t think Ohio’s Tate on X will be taking the ACT (for those who get the reference) but it would be nice to see the Wildcats put on a surprise show in Columbus. Drew Christmann (24-21 Northwestern ) Call me an optimist, but I’m going with Northwestern for this one. There’s no doubt that the last two weeks have been rough, and the Wildcats will once again be without Aidan Chiles. But I’m putting all of my chips on the running game this week. Northwestern has averaged 233 rushing yards per game in its six wins compared to 104 in the losses. I’m betting on Joseph Himon III and Caleb Komolafe, 8.4 and 5.8 yards per carry, respectively, to take the pressure off of Nicco Marchiol and keep the ball out of harms way. While Northwestern has been spiraling a bit, Ohio State has been right there with them. Since Julian Sayin went down, the Buckeyes have dropped from averaging 39.3 points in seven games to 23 in their last two, while giving up 71 points total. Replacement QB Luke Fahey is prone to mistakes, throwing three interceptions in those two games, and the run game didn’t help, managing just 53 yards last week against Oregon. The wild card is, of course, Jeremiah Smith, the likely No. 1 pick in this year’s draft, who can flip any game. Still, if Northwestern can control the clock and not give up too many big gains, I believe it can leave the Shoe with an upset. Donovan West (27-10 Ohio State ) There’s not much to say about this one. Ohio State has lost two games in a row and now hosts Northwestern in what is a must-win game for its playoff aspirations. The Buckeyes will come out hot, knowing they need to make a statement, with Nicco Marchiol in their way. Marchiol seems like a great person, but he’s simply not the playmaker and playextender that Chiles is. The ‘Cats will struggle to get anything going offensively against a defense riddled with five-stars, and OSU freshman backup quarterback Luke Fahey won’t be asked to do any more than hand the ball off and lob it over the top to Jeremiah Smith. Adam Sutro (34-17 Ohio State ) Last week, with Nicco Marchiol at the helm of the offense, Northwestern was completely ineffective offensively. After getting shut out in the first half of the ballgame, the ‘Cats finished with just 10 points. Its receivers couldn’t get separation on Iowa’s defensive backs and Marchiol was under duress all day long, forced to scramble 23 times. Fortunately, though Northwestern will be without starting quarterback Aidan Chiles for a second-straight weekend, the ‘Cats’ offensive outlook should improve in Columbus. Iowa has the best defense in the Big Ten, and though Ohio State’s is also good, it has been vulnerable in recent weeks. The Buckeyes have given up over 30 points in back-to-back weeks, in losses to USC and Oregon. So, I do think Northwestern will score a few more points than last week. But the bad news is that I don’t think it’ll have any defensive answer for Jeremiah Smith and Ohio State’s offense. With injuries still haunting NU’s secondary, expect Smith to finish will over 100 yards and a couple touchdowns in route to a double-digit Ohio State victory.

item.title: Mike Perry Inks 2027 UFC Return: 5 Fights We Need, Including Versus Conor McGregor
item.description: BKFC Over a 15-fight run in the UFC, Mike Perry created a solid fanbase for himself despite losing more than he won inside the Octagon. However, the man currently fighting out of Orlando, FL, became a far bigger name in combat sports during an outstanding six-fight stint with Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship , where he went unbeaten and won the promotion’s King of Violence title. Well, the 35-year-old has parlayed that new level of fame into an unexpected return to the UFC. On Friday, Perry revealed he had signed a multi-fight deal to return to the MMA world leader. Following the news, we look at five fights we need to see the “King of Violence” be a part of inside the Octagon in 2027 and beyond. Jorge Masvidal Mar 6, 2023; Miami, Florida, USA; American MMA fighter Jorge Masvidal attends the game between the Miami Heat and the Atlanta Hawks at Miami-Dade Arena. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-USA TODAY Sports For months, there have been reports that Jorge Masvidal was set to make his return to the UFC. However, a bout has yet to be announced. That isn’t too much of a surprise because at 42 years old, the company must be careful to avoid throwing the greybeard fighter into a tough matchup and maximize the little bit of relevance he has left. That is why Perry is the perfect foe. The bout is sure to be a 170-pound stand-up war, and both have advantages. Furthermore, a main event clash at a UFC Fight Night card in Florida could deliver strong numbers because of both men’s deep ties to the state. Joaquin Buckley May 9, 2026; Newark, New Jersey, UNITED STATES; Sean Brady (red gloves) fights Joaquin Buckley (blue gloves) during UFC 328 at Prudential Center. Mandatory Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images Perry needs to be matched up with fighters who will “stand and bang.” At least early in his second UFC run. Throwing him into bouts with talented grapplers would waste the sizable investment the UFC reportedly has in him. That is why another strong option as his return opponent would be Joaquin Buckley. After a serious hot streak, Buckley has lost three straight and is no longer in the title-fight conversation. A win over Perry would be good for him, while a clash with Buckley gives the returning star a name, ranked opponent that is a challenge and still a winnable bout. Conor McGregor Jul 11, 2026; Las Vegas, Nevada, USA; Conor McGregor (red gloves) is introduced before a welterweight bout against Max Holloway (not pictured) during UFC 329 at T-Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The fight many will clamor for is a scrap with UFC icon Conor McGregor . The Irishman has made it clear he wants to finish out the last fight on his UFC contract, then take his talents to the company he co-owns, BKFC. If the UFC wants to give Perry a winnable fight with a huge name, McGregor is perfect. But if they also want to give “Notorious” a chance to go out with one last win, the American is a great option as well. Furthermore, in a classic petty mane

Following the news, we look at five fights we need to see the “King of Violence” be a part of inside the Octagon in 2027 and beyond. Jorge Masvidal Mar 6, 2023; Miami, Florida, USA; American MMA fighter Jorge Masvidal attends the game between the Miami Heat and the Atlanta Hawks at Miami-Dade Arena. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-USA TODAY Sports For months, there have been reports that Jorge Masvidal was set to make his return to the UFC. However, a bout has yet to be announced. That isn’t too much of a surprise because at 42 years old, the company must be careful to avoid throwing the greybeard fighter into a tough matchup and maximize the little bit of relevance he has left. That is why Perry is the perfect foe. The bout is sure to be a 170-pound stand-up war, and both have advantages. Furthermore, a main event clash at a UFC Fight Night card in Florida could deliver strong numbers because of both men’s deep ties to the state. Joaquin Buckley May 9, 2026; Newark, New Jersey, UNITED STATES; Sean Brady (red gloves) fights Joaquin Buckley (blue gloves) during UFC 328 at Prudential Center. Mandatory Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images Perry needs to be matched up with fighters who will “stand and bang.” At least early in his second UFC run. Throwing him into bouts with talented grapplers would waste the sizable investment the UFC reportedly has in him. That is why another strong option as his return opponent would be Joaquin Buckley. After a serious hot streak, Buckley has lost three straight and is no longer in the title-fight conversation. A win over Perry would be good for him, while a clash with Buckley gives the returning star a name, ranked opponent that is a challenge and still a winnable bout. Conor McGregor Jul 11, 2026; Las Vegas, Nevada, USA; Conor McGregor (red gloves) is introduced before a welterweight bout against Max Holloway (not pictured) during UFC 329 at T-Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The fight many will clamor for is a scrap with UFC icon Conor McGregor . The Irishman has made it clear he wants to finish out the last fight on his UFC contract, then take his talents to the company he co-owns, BKFC. If the UFC wants to give Perry a winnable fight with a huge name, McGregor is perfect. But if they also want to give “Notorious” a chance to go out with one last win, the American is a great option as well. Furthermore, in a classic petty maneuver, the UFC could make the fight that McGregor and BKFC have wanted for a couple of years, but inside the Octagon instead of BKFC’s ring. Kevin Holland Apr 11, 2026; Miami, Florida, UNITED STATES; Kevin Holland (red gloves) fights Randy Brown (blue gloves) during UFC 327 at Kaseya Center. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Despite being in the company together for a few years and being highly active competitors, Mike Perry and Kevin Holland have never faced off inside the Octagon. That needs to end in “Platinum’s” second stint in the UFC. Both are highly entertaining fighters that talk trash. A matchup has Fight of the Year potential and would be another good option for a Perry UFC return fight in his adopted home of Orlando, FL. Renato Moicano Jun 28, 2025; Las Vegas, Nevada, USA; Beneil Dariush (red gloves) fights Renato Moicano (blue gloves) during UFC 317 at T-Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Stephen R. Sylvanie-Imagn Images One last option would be a matchup with top-15 lightweight Renato Moicano. After losing three of his last four, the Brazilian is not in line for any major matchups at 155 pounds. However, because of his willingness to fight anyone and cash in during his time in the sport, he would probably be open to moving up in weight to face Perry. Moicano would definitely have a speed and grappling advantage, but “Platinum’s” power would be a big problem and could help create a very exciting scrap.
