item.title: Lionel Scaloni addresses half-empty La Bombonera after Argentina's post-Messi era begins with Uruguay defeat
item.description: FBL-FRIENDLY-ARG-URU - AFP Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni has called for patience after his side suffered a 2-1 defeat to Uruguay in their first major outing since Lionel Messi’s retirement. The match was played in front of a noticeably sparse crowd at La Bombonera, marking a stark contrast to the usual atmosphere surrounding the world champions. Scaloni avoids attendance controversy The atmosphere at La Bombonera on Wednesday night was unusually quiet as Argentina faced Uruguay . Following the retirement of Messi, the national team appeared to lose some of its box-office appeal, with thousands of seats remaining empty for the clash. Scaloni, who recently committed his future to the team until 2030, was quick to downplay the significance of the low turnout during his post-match media duties. "I don't know how many people were there, I didn't even think about it. I don't have an opinion on that. I don't know what to tell you," Scaloni stated when questioned about the lack of supporters, as quoted by La Nacion . Boss insists loyalty outlasts the Messi era Despite the sobering sight of empty stands at La Bombonera, Argentina's coaching staff remains adamant that the deep-rooted bond between the national team and its supporters is unbreakable. While the sparse attendance in one of Buenos Aires' most iconic footballing strongholds hinted at the reality of a looming transitional era, the manager dismissed any suggestion that fan loyalty hinges solely on the presence of their talismanic number 10, Messi. "The people will surely come to cheer for the national team, they are unconditional, even if Leo is not playing. I have no doubt about that. We are the ones who have to inspire them. We cannot ask for more," the manager explained. Tactical analysis and Uruguay's dominance The match itself saw Argentina struggle to convert possession into clear chances. Uruguay took control shortly after the interval, scoring twice in six minutes through a Leonardo Balerdi own goal and a Maximiliano Araújo header. Although Julián Álvarez pulled one back in the 72nd minute, it was not enough to prevent a second consecutive victory for Diego Forlán’s side at the stadium of their historic rivals. Scaloni praised the visitors for their aggressive approach and tactical discipline. "Historically Uruguay is difficult, but for Argentina, Brazil, Spain and everyone. I congratulate them because they won well," he admitted. The Argentine boss also defended his decision not to throw on more attackers like Jose Manuel Lopez late in the game, citing the need to maintain tactical balance while Nico Paz was still performing well. Some may repeat because I think it is fair, which is what this is about, for them to play matches," he confirmed.

item.title: Tinubu met Nigeria in ICU – Mutfwang
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has said President Bola Tinubu met Nigeria in an intensive care unit, ICU, when he assumed office but has gradually moved the country into recovery through his administration’s policies. Mutfwang stated this on Saturday while speaking at the APC North-Central Presidential Campaign Rally at the Zaria Road Stadium, Jos, where he declared Plateau State’s support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 presidential election. The governor said, “You met Nigeria in the intensive care unit, and through the policies you have administered, like a drug, you have been able to bring Nigeria out of the intensive care unit. We are now in recovery. “We are confident that if you continue, we will not only recover but prosper as well. That is why we are determined that in the 2027 election, there is no alternative for us. We will stick with you and go with you.” He described Tinubu as a friend of Plateau State and the North-Central region, citing the Federal Government’s interventions in road infrastructure, education and healthcare. “We consider you as a friend of Plateau State and North-Central Nigeria in general. You have demonstrated your love for our state and our region through the developmental strides we have seen in road infrastructure, education and healthcare.” “On the Plateau, students in tertiary institutions have received assistance through the NELFUND scheme to the tune of over N11 billion. You have approved the road from Akwanga to Jos. You have also approved the road from Jos to Shendam, right through to Ebonyi. We are truly grateful,” he said. Mutfwang also commended the President’s wife, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, for her support to the people of Plateau State, recalling her visit to the state with gifts. “Your dear wife, our mother, is a darling of the Plateau people. We now know that we have a mother in Aso Rock. When she came visiting us, she did not come empty-handed. Like a good mother, she came with a bag full of gifts for our people, and we will always be grateful,” he said. You have approved the road from Akwanga to Jos. You have also approved the road from Jos to Shendam, right through to Ebonyi. We are truly grateful,” he said. Mutfwang also commended the President’s wife, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, for her support to the people of Plateau State, recalling her visit to the state with gifts. “Your dear wife, our mother, is a darling of the Plateau people. We now know that we have a mother in Aso Rock. When she came visiting us, she did not come empty-handed. Like a good mother, she came with a bag full of gifts for our people, and we will always be grateful,” he said. On presidential election Recalling his promise to reciprocate Tinubu’s kindness during the President’s previous visit, the governor said the time had come for Plateau people to demonstrate their appreciation through their votes. “The time has come and the time is now. By the grace of God, we are going to show our gratitude come January 16, 2027, because we have seen a man who loves us.” “When Plateau takes a direction, many other communities that share affinity with it will also follow suit. We are confident that the votes we will give Mr President in this election will be unprecedented,” he said. On security, Mutfwang commended the Federal Government for its support, saying the state had recorded significant progress in tackling insecurity in the last three months. “In the last three months particularly, we have made tremendous progress in dealing with insurgency. Like you have often said, we will defeat insurgency, and already we can see victory on the way.” “With commitment and sustainability, we will eliminate these enemies of peace and progress, and we are confident that you will lead us in that direction,” he said. The governor, however, appealed to Tinubu to support the state in facilitating the return of internally displaced persons to their ancestral communities. “We will continue to solicit your help, Mr President, to make sure that our people who are internally displaced return to their ancestral homes. “We will be approaching you with a Marshall Plan for the return of our people to their ancestral homes. It is going to require substantial intervention from you, and we are confident that what you have done before, you will do again,” he said. Mutfwang also appealed to the President to assist in completing the Zaria Road Stadium, describing it as a facility whose construction began about 40 years ago. “Mr President, I will be pleading with you on behalf of the Plateau people. Please roll away our reproach. We need your help to make this stadium one of the international stadiums in Nigeria. I am sure it will become a symbol of pride for you when this is done,” he said He further disclosed that his administration had established an employment hub expected to provide jobs for 2,000 young people, alongside a technology hub designed to support security operations. “We have created an employment hub for 2,000 young people who will be working in America and Europe from the comfort of their homes here in Jos. “We have also created another hub for technology so that we can deploy effective technology for the detection of criminals,” he said. The governor added that additional buses had been procured to ease transportation challenges facing residents of the state. item.title: Mark Your Calendars! Lagos International Theatre Festival Returns to MUSON Centre This November
item.description: The Lagos International Theatre Festival ( LITF ) returns for its 2026 edition on November 14–15 at the MUSON Centre, Lagos, bringing together an exciting programme of theatre from Nigeria and around the world. The festival, which attracts more than 25,000 attendees across its programme days, has become one of the most anticipated events on Lagos’s cultural calendar. This year’s festival is themed “The Masks We Wear”, anchored by the statement “The Stage Is Everywhere.” The theme explores the different roles and identities people assume in everyday life, while inviting audiences to consider how theatre extends beyond the traditional stage. LITF 2026 brings an international dimension to Lagos, featuring artists and productions from Kenya, Canada and Brazil alongside a diverse Nigerian programme. An international highlight is LeRa Entertainments’ Under The Mango Tree from Canada, produced by Lennette Randall , with productions from Norway, Kenya and Brazil adding further cultural and theatrical perspectives. The Nigerian programme features productions from Lagos, Abuja, Enugu and Abeokuta, including Monkey Laundry , directed by Olarotimi Fakunle ; tHERapy , directed by Tosin Adeyemi ; What You Have Become , directed by Lanre Adediwura; and Behind Closed Doors , directed by Bolanle Austen-Peters. The festival will also spotlight emerging theatre makers through productions from Atlantic Hall, Evergreen College and Children’s International School, alongside professional and independent productions. The festival experience begins ahead of the main weekend with a series of events across Lagos. On November 9, Theatre Meets Food, hosted by Hilda Baci, will bring together artists, partners, cultural leaders and members of Lagos’s creative community for an evening of food, theatre and conversation. This will be followed by Embassy Nights on November 10 and 11, celebrating international cultural exchange among diplomatic representatives, artists and creative industry leaders. The programme culminates in an Opening Night Gala on November 13, ahead of the main festival weekend at MUSON Centre on November 14 and 15. LITF 2026 is supported by the Lagos State Government, LekOil, Pillar Oil, Afrexim and Amstel , alongside its growing network of international and cultural partners. Founder of LITF, Bolanle Austen-Peters , said: “The Masks We Wear is a theme that speaks to all of us. We all play different roles in our lives, and theatre allows us to examine those roles, question them, and perhaps see ourselves differently. This year, we are also reminding audiences that theatre is not confined to a theatre building. item.dc:creator: BellaNaija.com
item.content:encoded: The Lagos International Theatre Festival ( LITF ) returns for its 2026 edition on November 14–15 at the MUSON Centre, Lagos, bringing together an exciting programme of theatre from Nigeria and around the world. The festival, which attracts more than 25,000 attendees across its programme days, has become one of the most anticipated events on Lagos’s cultural calendar. This year’s festival is themed “The Masks We Wear”, anchored by the statement “The Stage Is Everywhere.” The theme explores the different roles and identities people assume in everyday life, while inviting audiences to consider how theatre extends beyond the traditional stage. LITF 2026 brings an international dimension to Lagos, featuring artists and productions from Kenya, Canada and Brazil alongside a diverse Nigerian programme. An international highlight is LeRa Entertainments’ Under The Mango Tree from Canada, produced by Lennette Randall , with productions from Norway, Kenya and Brazil adding further cultural and theatrical perspectives. The Nigerian programme features productions from Lagos, Abuja, Enugu and Abeokuta, including Monkey Laundry , directed by Olarotimi Fakunle ; tHERapy , directed by Tosin Adeyemi ; What You Have Become , directed by Lanre Adediwura; and Behind Closed Doors , directed by Bolanle Austen-Peters. The festival will also spotlight emerging theatre makers through productions from Atlantic Hall, Evergreen College and Children’s International School, alongside professional and independent productions. The festival experience begins ahead of the main weekend with a series of events across Lagos. On November 9, Theatre Meets Food, hosted by Hilda Baci, will bring together artists, partners, cultural leaders and members of Lagos’s creative community for an evening of food, theatre and conversation. This will be followed by Embassy Nights on November 10 and 11, celebrating international cultural exchange among diplomatic representatives, artists and creative industry leaders. The programme culminates in an Opening Night Gala on November 13, ahead of the main festival weekend at MUSON Centre on November 14 and 15. LITF 2026 is supported by the Lagos State Government, LekOil, Pillar Oil, Afrexim and Amstel , alongside its growing network of international and cultural partners. Founder of LITF, Bolanle Austen-Peters , said: “The Masks We Wear is a theme that speaks to all of us. We all play different roles in our lives, and theatre allows us to examine those roles, question them, and perhaps see ourselves differently. This year, we are also reminding audiences that theatre is not confined to a theatre building. The stage is everywhere.” Festival Director, Vanessa Jev , said the diversity of voices at this year’s festival was particularly exciting, with Nigerian artists joining performers from Kenya, Canada and Brazil to create opportunities for audiences to experience different cultures and perspectives. Founded by Bolanle Austen-Peters, LITF celebrates theatre and performance while showcasing Nigerian creativity and fostering international collaboration, cultural exchange and artistic dialogue. item.title: Otti, Ajaero, others pay tributes to late NLC scribe, Ugboaja
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — It was a night of tears, fond memories and glowing tributes on Friday as labour leaders, government officials, family members and associates gathered in Umuahia to celebrate the life and legacy of the late Secretary-General of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Comrade Emmanuel Okechukwu Ugboaja. Ugboaja, who hailed from Nkpa in Bende Local Government Area of Abia State, died at the age of 60. At the Night of Tributes organised by the Abia State Government at the International Conference Centre, Umuahia, speakers took turns to recount the late labour leader’s contributions to workers’ welfare, organised labour and humanity, describing his death as an irreparable loss. Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, who led the tributes, described Ugboaja’s death as painful, but said his contributions to the labour movement and society would remain an enduring legacy. Otti particularly celebrated his emergence as the first and only indigene of Abia State to occupy the position of NLC Secretary-General among the five individuals who had held the office. “Out of the five Secretaries-General of the Nigeria Labour Congress, Comrade Emmanuel Ugboaja was the only one from Abia State. “He was the first NLC Secretary-General from our State, and that is a significant achievement,” the governor said. Reflecting on the meaning of life, Otti said a person’s worth was not measured by the number of years spent on earth but by the positive impact made and the legacies left behind. He expressed confidence that the late Ugboaja had successfully fulfilled his earthly assignment, urging his family not to surrender to despair but to draw strength from the Christian hope of resurrection. “From everything we have heard about him today, we have no doubt that Comrade Emmanuel Ugboaja finished his race here on earth. There are no mistakes with God. “We urge the family not to mourn like those without hope. Our prayer is that on the resurrection morning, when the trumpet shall sound, Comrade Emmanuel Ugboaja will be among those who will rise to eternal life,” Otti said. The governor prayed for the peaceful repose of the deceased’s soul and journey mercies for those who attended the event. In his tribute, NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero, described Ugboaja as a committed labour activist and a worthy son of the workers’ movement. Ajaero recalled that their relationship dated back to 1993, when both were actively involved in their respective professional and union activities. He described the deceased as a man of strong convictions who remained steadfast in the struggle for workers’ rights and made significant contributions to the growth of organised labour. The NLC president urged members of the labour movement and others who encountered Ugboaja to preserve his memory and sustain his legacy, noting that his death was another reminder of the fleeting nature of human existence. Reflecting on the meaning of life, Otti said a person’s worth was not measured by the number of years spent on earth but by the positive impact made and the legacies left behind. He expressed confidence that the late Ugboaja had successfully fulfilled his earthly assignment, urging his family not to surrender to despair but to draw strength from the Christian hope of resurrection. “From everything we have heard about him today, we have no doubt that Comrade Emmanuel Ugboaja finished his race here on earth. There are no mistakes with God. “We urge the family not to mourn like those without hope. Our prayer is that on the resurrection morning, when the trumpet shall sound, Comrade Emmanuel Ugboaja will be among those who will rise to eternal life,” Otti said. The governor prayed for the peaceful repose of the deceased’s soul and journey mercies for those who attended the event. In his tribute, NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero, described Ugboaja as a committed labour activist and a worthy son of the workers’ movement. Ajaero recalled that their relationship dated back to 1993, when both were actively involved in their respective professional and union activities. He described the deceased as a man of strong convictions who remained steadfast in the struggle for workers’ rights and made significant contributions to the growth of organised labour. The NLC president urged members of the labour movement and others who encountered Ugboaja to preserve his memory and sustain his legacy, noting that his death was another reminder of the fleeting nature of human existence. In their respective tributes, TUC Secretary, Engr. Festus Osifu; Abia State NLC Chairman, Comrade Okoro Ogbonaya; and other labour stakeholders joined workers across the country in mourning the late unionist. They described him as humble, remarkable, eloquent and a blessing to humanity, the Nkpa community and Abia State, lamenting that his death had created a huge vacuum in the labour movement. They prayed God to comfort his family and grant them the fortitude to bear the loss. Speaking on behalf of the family, the deceased’s brother, Mr Patrick Ugboaja, described him as a national and international figure who, despite his towering profile, never lost touch with his roots. He recalled that beyond his demanding responsibilities in the labour movement, the late Ugboaja was also a farmer, devoted family man and friendly personality who related freely with people, irrespective of their backgrounds. Patrick expressed deep appreciation to Governor Otti, the Abia State Government and everyone who had stood by the family during their difficult period. Speaking on behalf of the younger generation of the family, the deceased’s son, Emmanuel Ugboaja Jnr., remembered his father as a disciplined man who understood the need to strike a balance between professional responsibilities and recreation. He said the values of discipline, focus, hard work and determination consistently instilled by his father had become enduring lessons for him and his younger siblings. He also recalled his father’s generosity and selfless disposition, particularly his commitment to helping others. Earlier, in a sermon titled, “Before the Translation: What Will Be Your Testimony?”, drawn from Hebrews 11:5, Very Rev. Dr Emmanuel Chukwuma challenged the congregation to live purposeful lives and leave behind positive testimonies before their departure from the world. The cleric also commended Governor Otti for his developmental efforts in Abia State, expressing optimism about the governor’s second-term ambition. The Night of Tributes attracted labour leaders from within and outside Nigeria, government functionaries, family members, friends and associates, who gathered to honour the memory of a man whose influence extended beyond the workplace into the wider society. Ugboaja is scheduled to be buried on Saturday after a funeral service at Amohoro Nkpa, his country home. item.title: Clashes between gangs, vigilantes kill over 50 in Zamfara – Report
item.description: Clashes between criminal gangs and local vigilantes have left more than 50 people dead in northwestern Nigeria’s Zamfara state, residents told AFP Saturday. Zamfara is one of several states in northwest and central Nigeria terrorised by kidnapping-for-ransom and cattle-rustling gangs who raid villages, kill and abduct residents as well as looting homes before burning them. Locals call the gangs bandits. Vigilantes from Zoma village in Bukkuyum district ambushed the bandits who were passing through the village on Thursday after kidnapping several people from nearby Gummi district, the sources said. “We were alerted that the bandits were heading our way, so our vigilantes laid in wait for the bandits and engaged them in a fierce gunfight,” said a traditional village chief who asked not to be identified for personal safety. “Our vigilantes killed 44 of the bandits … we also lost nine vigilantes in the fight,” said the chief, adding that a notorious bandit commander called Jijji, who had led the kidnapping, was also killed in the fight. – Call for weapons – News of bandit attacks in remote areas is usually slow to emerge due to poor telecommunications and distance. A Zamfara state police spokesman contacted by AFP said the force had yet to receive details about the clashes. Zoma residents Kabiru Tafida and Basiru Buhari reached by AFP gave the same account of the clashes and toll. “We call on the authorities to provide our vigilantes with guns and ammunition to fight these bandits who use sophisticated weapons,” Buhari said. Banditry in Africa’s most populous country traces its roots to conflicts between herders and farmers over access to limited land and water, made worse by climate change and population growth. Out of the violence emerged powerful gangs, largely composed of Fulani herders — and a kidnapping economy, while at times forging alliances with jihadists. In Zamfara’s neighbouring state Katsina, a bandit leader recently told AFP that “years of injustices” drove him and other cattle herders into banditry. He spoke during a rare interview which came during the reporting of an article for The New York Review of Books, co-authored by an American academic and writer Helen Epstein and an AFP northern Nigeria reporter. The Nigerian military routinely refers to bandits as “terrorists”, and runs a dedicated military campaign in the northwest to combat them. Worsening insecurity and the high cost of living have become major issues in the ongoing presidential campaign, as Bola Tinubu runs for a second term in January polls. item.title: Raphinha sees red as Brazil stunned by Japan while Argentina’s post-Messi era starts with defeat
item.description: Loss in Singapore marred by unruly end to friendly Argentina beaten 2-1 by Uruguay in Buenos Aires Raphinha was sent off as Brazil crashed to a 3-2 defeat to Japan in their international friendly in Singapore. The Barcelona captain had been substituted after 71 minutes, but was shown a red card after protesting against Tatsuhiro Sakamoto’s stoppage-time winner on the touchline. The Brazil head coach, Carlo Ancelotti, was also sent off in a fractious ending to the match. Japan went 2-0 up inside 20 minutes through Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura. Vinicius Junior reduced the deficit in the 33rd minute and scored again to drag them level on 75 minutes, before Sakamoto’s controversial late winner. Continue reading...

item.title: Her Enterprise, Africa’s Advantage: HerSphere Global Summit 2026 Convenes Africa’s Foremost Women Leaders in Lagos
item.description: Africa’s economic story is increasingly being written by women. Across the continent, women own and operate a remarkable share of small and growing enterprises, sustain household and community economies, and drive innovation in sectors from finance and technology to the creative industries. Yet the gap between participation and power remains wide. Too many women-led businesses stay small, under-capitalised and absent from the rooms where markets, policy and capital are shaped. On Tuesday, 17 November 2026, the HerSphere Global Summit 2026 will gather a distinguished assembly of leaders at the Wole Soyinka Centre, Lagos, Nigeria, to confront that gap directly. Proceedings begin promptly at 9:00 a.m. A Theme That Demands Action This year’s theme, “ Her Enterprise, Africa Advantage: Moving Women-Led Businesses Beyond Participation to Economic Power,” reflects a deliberate shift in the conversation. The question is no longer whether women belong in Africa’s economy — that has long been settled. The question is how women-led enterprises can scale, command capital, influence policy and build institutions that endure. The summit is designed to move beyond inspiration to strategy: how women founders access growth finance, how they enter regional and global value chains, how public institutions and private capital can work together to back them, and how today’s enterprises become tomorrow’s market leaders. An Exceptional Line-Up of Voices HerSphere Global Summit 2026 brings together an exceptional roster of women who have shaped Nigeria’s and Africa’s judicial, public, financial, entrepreneurial and creative landscapes: • Hon. Justice Amina Adamu Augie (CFR) • Dolapo Osinbajo • Hannatu Musa Musawa • Godrey Ogbechie • Maisie Dunbar • Bolanle Austen-Peters • Uche Pedro • Jumoke Olaniyan • Monisola Olufunke Alabi • Brenda Nwagwu • Chioma Ude • Adesuwa Okunbo Rhodes • Ifeoma Uddoh • Temilade Aduroja • Lehle Balde • Arese Ugwu Together, they represent decades of leadership across law, public service, investment, media, entertainment, financial inclusion and enterprise building — and a shared conviction that Africa’s prosperity depends on the full economic power of its women. Backed by Institutions That Shape the Economy The summit is supported by a strong coalition of partners: the Lagos State Government, the Office of Sustainable Development Goals (Lagos Global), the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX), Delphino Entertainment, and SheMeansBusiness by BusinessDay. Their involvement underscores a growing recognition across government, capital markets and media that empowering women-led enterprise is not a social side-project — it is core economic strategy. Who Should Attend HerSphere Global Summit 2026 is for: • Women founders and business owners ready to scale • Investors, financiers and capital-market leaders seeking high-potential opportunities • Policymakers and development partners committed to inclusive growth • Corporate executives building diverse supply chai

item.description: null SpaceX plans to catch the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), and you can watch the action live. Starship launched on its 15th test flight on Friday evening (Nov. 13), rising into the sky from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. The mission plan called for bringing both of the vehicle's stages back to Starbase and catching them with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — an unprecedented total recovery of an orbital rocket . That didn't happen, however; SpaceX diverted Starship's Super Heavy booster to a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico 6.5 minutes after launch. (SpaceX said later that a guidance and navigaton issue during its descent triggered and automatic abort. The materials here are alloy steel and it weighs just 225g. You can watch it live here at Space.com. There's no guarantee that it will happen, however: If SpaceX detects anything off-nominal with Ship, it will scrap the catch attempt, as it did with Super Heavy on Friday afternoon. We'll just have to wait and see. SpaceX, however, seems confident. That didn't happen, however; SpaceX diverted Starship's Super Heavy booster to a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico 6.5 minutes after launch. (SpaceX said later that a guidance and navigaton issue during its descent triggered and automatic abort. But a catch of the Ship upper stage is still on the table, and that would be historic in itself: SpaceX has never tried it before. Starship Die Cast Rocket Model Was $47.99 Now $39.99 on Amazon . Even if you can't see SpaceX's Starship in person, you can score a model of your own. Standing at 13.77 inches (35 cm), this is a 1:375 ratio of SpaceX's Starship as a desktop model. The materials here are alloy steel and it weighs just 225g. View Deal The Ship catch is scheduled to occur today at around 4:20 p.m. EST (2120 GMT; 3:20 p.m. local Texas time) — roughly 22.5 hours after Flight 15 lifted off. You can watch it live here at Space.com. There's no guarantee that it will happen, however: If SpaceX detects anything off-nominal with Ship, it will scrap the catch attempt, as it did with Super Heavy on Friday afternoon. We'll just have to wait and see. SpaceX, however, seems confident. Flight controllers decided early Saturday morning, about seven hours after liftoff, to forgo a second window to end the mission early with a splashdown off the coast of Chile. "Starship's going to stay in space. We are one step closer to an eventual return to launch site," SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot said in a live commentary update. "So that's great news." The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket circles Earth on Flight 15 on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) While the double-catch attempt was Flight 15's main headline, the mission had other objectives as well. One was getting Ship to orbit, which had happened on just one previous Starship launch — Flight 14 , which lifted off on Sept. 28. Ship deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 broadband satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) on Flight 14, and it did so again on Flight 15. These 52 spacecraft are the first members of a constellation that will eventually consist of 100,000 satellites , if all goes according to SpaceX's plan. Some of those Starlink satellites took video and images of Starship's heat shield to check its health for today's landing attempt. Those images, combined with ground-based cameras, found the Ship in good shape. the company said. "Our heat shield team reviewed all the data we got from our ground tracking cameras, and from those satellite cameras and confirmed the heat shield is in a good posture for a reentry and return to the launch site," Huot said. And SpaceX plans to use Starship to build an even bigger network in LEO — Starmind, an AI data-center constellation that will harbor a million spacecraft , according to Elon Musk . (For context: SpaceX's current-gen Starlink network employs about 11,000 satellites at the moment.) Assembling these megaconstellations will require an incredible launch cadence. And the double chopstick catch is key to that vision, SpaceX says, for it will enable quicker inspection, refurbishment and reflight of Starship. So the company will doubtless try the maneuver again soon — probably on the next Starship flight, which won't be too far down the road. Editor's note: This story was updated at 8 a.m. EST to include new details on SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 mission from SpaceX. Space.com Editor-in-Chief Tariq Malik contributed to this report.

item.title: 2027: Why Peter Obi could win presidential election
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA- AHEAD of next year’s elections, the National leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, has already predicted an overwhelming victory for its presidential candidate, Peter Obi. They said the platform presents a formidable pathway to victory for the party. Read Also: * 2027: Why Tinubu may still win presidential election * 2027: Why Atiku could win presidential election The party said both the South-East and South-South are firmly blocked, and the North-West and North-East are equally blocked for Obi/ Kwankwaso for January 16, 2027 presidential election. According to the NDC, the 2023 election already demonstrated Obi’s clear electoral strength across the North-Central, where he carried Plateau, Nasarawa, and the FCT, stressing that Nigerians are ready to look past incumbency and deliver a decisive mandate for Peter Obi and the NDC. Speaking with Vanguard exclusively, the spokesperson, NDC National Campaign Council, Dr. Chiogo Constance Ikokwu said those who mistake Peter Obi’s gentlemanly demeanor for weakness overlook what she described as the grit and resilience of a leader who grew up navigating the tough, street-smart realities of Onitsha. The NDC National Campaign Council Spokesperson said another major advantage for the party that would contribute to its victory next year is that Kwankwasiyya movement is no pushover when it comes to electoral sturdiness against the backdrop that the group had been tested, it is a disciplined one and ready to defend its mandate at the polls. Ikokwu, who noted that no sensible election rigger would wish to confront the potent combination of the Obidient and Kwankwasiyya (OK) movements, stressed that as many voters demonstrated in the previous cycle, financial inducements on election day will not stop struggling citizens from voting their conscience, adding that Nigerians are ready to look past incumbency and deliver a decisive mandate for Peter Obi and the NDC. The NDC said Obi will win the presidential election despite the fact that critics often point to the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, boasting over 30 aligned state governors as an insurmountable advantage, stressing that Nigerian political history had proven it that governors do not cast votes, but citizens do. item.content:encoded: By Henry Umoru ABUJA- AHEAD of next year’s elections, the National leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, has already predicted an overwhelming victory for its presidential candidate, Peter Obi. They said the platform presents a formidable pathway to victory for the party. Read Also: * 2027: Why Tinubu may still win presidential election * 2027: Why Atiku could win presidential election The party said both the South-East and South-South are firmly blocked, and the North-West and North-East are equally blocked for Obi/ Kwankwaso for January 16, 2027 presidential election. According to the NDC, the 2023 election already demonstrated Obi’s clear electoral strength across the North-Central, where he carried Plateau, Nasarawa, and the FCT, stressing that Nigerians are ready to look past incumbency and deliver a decisive mandate for Peter Obi and the NDC. Speaking with Vanguard exclusively, the spokesperson, NDC National Campaign Council, Dr. Chiogo Constance Ikokwu said those who mistake Peter Obi’s gentlemanly demeanor for weakness overlook what she described as the grit and resilience of a leader who grew up navigating the tough, street-smart realities of Onitsha. The NDC National Campaign Council Spokesperson said another major advantage for the party that would contribute to its victory next year is that Kwankwasiyya movement is no pushover when it comes to electoral sturdiness against the backdrop that the group had been tested, it is a disciplined one and ready to defend its mandate at the polls. Ikokwu, who noted that no sensible election rigger would wish to confront the potent combination of the Obidient and Kwankwasiyya (OK) movements, stressed that as many voters demonstrated in the previous cycle, financial inducements on election day will not stop struggling citizens from voting their conscience, adding that Nigerians are ready to look past incumbency and deliver a decisive mandate for Peter Obi and the NDC. The NDC said Obi will win the presidential election despite the fact that critics often point to the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, boasting over 30 aligned state governors as an insurmountable advantage, stressing that Nigerian political history had proven it that governors do not cast votes, but citizens do. According to the NDC, In 2015, an incumbent president backed by the vast majority of state governors was defeated at the polls, and even in 2023, President Bola Tinubu lost key states where his most enthusiastic governors held sway, including Lagos, Kaduna under Nasir El-Rufai, and Imo. The NDC spokesperson said: “The 2027 Nigerian presidential election is shaping up not merely as a contest between political parties, but as a decisive referendum between entrenched incumbency and the survival of ordinary citizens. “Looking closely at the political mathematics, grassroots momentum, and prevailing economic realities, the joint ticket of Peter Obi and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso on the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presents a formidable pathway to victory. “First, the sheer electoral arithmetic of an Obi–Kwankwaso alliance fundamentally alters Nigeria’s political landscape. In 2023, running separately without the backing of a single sitting state governor, Peter Obi won 12 states, including the Federal Capital Territory, on the strength of an organic, youth-driven Obidient movement across the South and North-Central. “Also consider that while INEC officially declared Tinubu the winner of Rivers State, Nigerians know who truly won that state. The Kwakwanso factor “Meanwhile, Rabiu Kwankwaso commanded a disciplined, revolutionary Kwankwasiyya grassroots network that dominated Kano and resonated deeply across the core North. Uniting these two massive, people-powered movements under the NDC bridges Nigeria’s traditional North–South divide, creating a broad coalition that rivals any political machine in Nigerian presidential history.” Ikokwu further said, “Unlike the Obi-Kwankwaso alliance, the Tinubu-Shettima ticket faces no viable path to victory. Both the South-East and South-South are firmly blocked, and the North-West and North-East are equally blocked. Moreover, the 2023 election already demonstrated Obi’s clear electoral strength across the North-Central, where he carried Plateau, Nasarawa, and the FCT. “Critics often point to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) boasting over 30 aligned state governors as an insurmountable advantage. Yet Nigerian political history proves that governors do not cast votes—citizens do. In 2015, an incumbent president backed by the vast majority of state governors was defeated at the polls, and even in 2023, President Bola Tinubu lost key states where his most enthusiastic governors held sway, including Lagos, Kaduna under Nasir El-Rufai, and Imo. “Equally, the Kwankwasiyya movement is no pushover when it comes to electoral sturdiness; the group is tested, disciplined, and ready to defend its mandate at the polls. “Simply put, no sensible election rigger would wish to confront the potent combination of the Obidient and Kwankwasiyya (OK) movements. Unlike in 2023, when organizational gaps left opposition tallies vulnerable, the NDC is actively building disciplined, lawful structures to guard and protect every ballot across Nigeria’s 176,000 polling units. “Backed by over 200 million citizens determined to stand firm at the polls through peaceful civic vigilance and overwhelming turnout, intimidation or vote-buying will not override the will of the Nigerian people. As many voters demonstrated in the previous cycle, financial inducements on election day will not stop struggling citizens from voting their conscience. Economy “Above all, 2027 is a battle between the ruling establishment and millions of suffering Nigerians. Never in Nigeria’s peacetime history has the cost of basic human survival escalated by over 500 percent in such a short span. Staple foods have slipped out of reach, with a bag of rice surging from roughly ₦15,000 to over ₦70,000, while relentless fuel price hikes have crippled transportation, small businesses, and household incomes. Speaking on debt burden exceeding $120 billion by the present government as an advantage for Peter Obi to win the election, the NDC spokesperson said, “Simultaneously, the administration has presided over a total public debt burden exceeding $120 billion, alongside an independent inquiry into how borrowed funds and subsidy savings have been managed, without delivering tangible improvements in power supply, healthcare, or security. Today, no one is safe in Nigeria, thanks to President Tinubu. Nigerians are not fools. “They will cast their votes recognizing that President Tinubu failed to keep his 2023 campaign promises, and they are set to hold him accountable at the ballot box for the reckless manner in which he removed the fuel subsidy, a decision that has brought average citizens to their knees. At the polls, voters will demand a clear answer: Where are the savings from the removal of the fuel subsidy? That is, where is our money that Peter Obi has been asking?” Citing insecurity and hunger in the as parameters that will work against the President Tinubu led government, Ikokwu said, “Nowhere will the political fallout of this hardship be felt more acutely than in Northern Nigeria, where acute hunger and persistent insecurity have pushed communities to the brink. Beyond immediate survival, Northern voters are also weighing the strategic question of 2031 and national leadership succession, comparing the proven grassroots loyalty and developmental record of Kwankwaso alongside Obi against the current administration’s trajectory. “Ultimately, 2027 offers Nigerians a stark choice: between a ticket anchored in verifiable enterprise, prudence, and transparent wealth creation, and an incumbent establishment burdened by economic hardship and long-standing controversies over the origins of its wealth

item.title: ADC: Atiku hasn’t reached out to me despite coming from the same zone – Nafiu Bala
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo A factional leader of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Nafiu Bala Gombe, has expressed disappointment that former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has not personally reached out to him despite their coming from the same geopolitical zone. Bala, who spoke in an interview with BBC Hausa on Saturday, said he regarded Atiku as a father figure but was disappointed that the former vice-president had not contacted him amid the leadership crisis rocking the party. He said this while reacting to a court judgment that affirmed his faction’s position in the ADC leadership dispute, adding that he remained willing to work with Atiku, former Senate President David Mark and other party chieftains to strengthen the opposition ahead of the 2027 general elections. Bala said the judgment had vindicated his faction as the authentic leadership of the party, insisting that its position was based on the provisions of the ADC constitution. “Alhamdulillah. As we always say, truth is truth, while lies remain lies. Allah has vindicated us. The court has seen the merit of our case and our truthfulness and has decided to return the party leadership to us,” he said. He disclosed that his faction was awaiting the Certified True Copy of the judgment to enable it to approach the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) for the necessary changes to the party’s leadership records. Bala, however, cautioned against interpreting the judgment as an opportunity to settle scores with members of the opposing faction, saying he was extending a hand of friendship to them. “This is not a fight. Allah has given us victory, but we are not enemies. We are extending a hand of friendship to them to stop being arrogant and whatever they may say, so that we can strengthen the opposition and face the government,” he said. He maintained that anyone seeking to join the ADC or contest an elective position on its platform must comply with the party’s constitution, particularly provisions governing membership registration, payment of dues and eligibility for leadership positions. According to him, the party’s constitution requires members to fulfil prescribed conditions, including two years of membership and payment of stipulated dues, before qualifying for leadership positions. He alleged that the opposing faction failed to follow the party’s membership registration procedures, claiming that David Mark obtained his membership card from a former national chairman in Abuja rather than registering at his ward. Bala said he had repeatedly warned the opposing group about the consequences of disregarding the party’s constitution, but his advice was ignored. item.content:encoded: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo A factional leader of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Nafiu Bala Gombe, has expressed disappointment that former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has not personally reached out to him despite their coming from the same geopolitical zone. Bala, who spoke in an interview with BBC Hausa on Saturday, said he regarded Atiku as a father figure but was disappointed that the former vice-president had not contacted him amid the leadership crisis rocking the party. He said this while reacting to a court judgment that affirmed his faction’s position in the ADC leadership dispute, adding that he remained willing to work with Atiku, former Senate President David Mark and other party chieftains to strengthen the opposition ahead of the 2027 general elections. Bala said the judgment had vindicated his faction as the authentic leadership of the party, insisting that its position was based on the provisions of the ADC constitution. “Alhamdulillah. As we always say, truth is truth, while lies remain lies. Allah has vindicated us. The court has seen the merit of our case and our truthfulness and has decided to return the party leadership to us,” he said. He disclosed that his faction was awaiting the Certified True Copy of the judgment to enable it to approach the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) for the necessary changes to the party’s leadership records. Bala, however, cautioned against interpreting the judgment as an opportunity to settle scores with members of the opposing faction, saying he was extending a hand of friendship to them. “This is not a fight. Allah has given us victory, but we are not enemies. We are extending a hand of friendship to them to stop being arrogant and whatever they may say, so that we can strengthen the opposition and face the government,” he said. He maintained that anyone seeking to join the ADC or contest an elective position on its platform must comply with the party’s constitution, particularly provisions governing membership registration, payment of dues and eligibility for leadership positions. According to him, the party’s constitution requires members to fulfil prescribed conditions, including two years of membership and payment of stipulated dues, before qualifying for leadership positions. He alleged that the opposing faction failed to follow the party’s membership registration procedures, claiming that David Mark obtained his membership card from a former national chairman in Abuja rather than registering at his ward. Bala said he had repeatedly warned the opposing group about the consequences of disregarding the party’s constitution, but his advice was ignored. He also dismissed allegations that he was being used by the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to destabilise the opposition, insisting that his court action was solely aimed at protecting his rights and upholding the ADC constitution. “I went to court with only the constitution. I told the world that if they had followed the right procedures, the court should rule in their favour. But if we were right, we should be given our rights,” he said. On the continued appearance of Atiku’s and David Mark’s names on INEC’s portal, Bala said the commission would act appropriately once it received the Certified True Copy of the judgment. He dismissed suggestions that INEC was deliberately delaying the implementation of the judgment, saying the commission might not have received the official court document. Bala also rejected arguments that the large crowds attracted by the ADC during political engagements in Sokoto and Kebbi states should have persuaded him to abandon the legal battle. READ ALSO: I went to court to defend my rights, not working for APC to destabilise opposition — Nafiu Bala He argued that political popularity and financial influence should not be used to justify disregard for the law, warning that the country could not make progress if influential politicians continued to violate established rules. The factional leader further claimed that some individuals involved in the dispute had circulated documents suggesting that he had resigned from his position, describing the claims as misleading. On the party’s preparations for the 2027 elections, Bala said his faction had directed all aspirants seeking elective positions on the ADC platform to continue their campaign activities. He urged members of the opposing faction to remain patient, follow the party’s constitutional procedures and complete their membership registration at their respective wards. On funding, he said his faction relied largely on membership dues and other contributions generated through the party’s internal activities. Bala also defended his security arrangements and lifestyle, saying he was entitled to protection like other prominent political figures. He added that he was a businessman with other sources of livelihood. He urged Nigerian youths to remain law-abiding and avoid being drawn into political confrontations, stressing that opposition politics should be conducted with respect for democratic institutions and the rule of law. item.title: I went to court to defend my rights, not working for APC to destabilise opposition — Nafiu Bala
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo A factional leader of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Nafiu Bala Gombe, has dismissed allegations that he is working for the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to destabilise the opposition, insisting that his legal action against the party’s rival leadership was aimed solely at defending his rights and upholding the party’s constitution. Bala also extended an olive branch to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, former Senate President David Mark and other party chieftains following a court judgment that affirmed his faction’s position in the ADC leadership dispute. Speaking on BBC Hausa on Saturday, Bala said the judgment had vindicated his faction as the authentic leadership of the party, maintaining that its legal position was based on the provisions of the ADC constitution. “Alhamdulillah. As we always say, truth is truth, while lies remain lies. Allah has vindicated us. The court has seen the merit of our case and our truthfulness and has decided to return the party leadership to us,” he said. He disclosed that his faction was awaiting the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the judgment before approaching the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to effect the necessary changes to the party’s leadership records. Bala, however, said the judgment should not be regarded as an opportunity to settle scores with the opposing faction, expressing his willingness to work with Atiku, Mark and other prominent politicians to strengthen the opposition ahead of the 2027 general elections. “This is not a fight. Allah has given us victory, but we are not enemies. We are extending a hand of friendship to them to stop being arrogant and whatever they may say, so that we can strengthen the opposition and face the government,” he said. Addressing the allegations that he was being sponsored to weaken the opposition, Bala insisted that he approached the court based on the party’s constitution and was prepared to accept any judgment delivered in accordance with the law. “I went to court with only the constitution. I told the world that if they had followed the right procedures, the court should rule in their favour. But if we were right, we should be given our rights,” he said. The ADC factional leader maintained that anyone seeking to join the party or contest elective positions on its platform must comply with its constitutional provisions, particularly those governing ward registration, membership dues and eligibility for leadership positions. According to him, the party’s constitution requires members to fulfil specified conditions, including two years of membership and payment of stipulated dues, before becoming eligible for leadership positions. Addressing the allegations that he was being sponsored to weaken the opposition, Bala insisted that he approached the court based on the party’s constitution and was prepared to accept any judgment delivered in accordance with the law. “I went to court with only the constitution. I told the world that if they had followed the right procedures, the court should rule in their favour. But if we were right, we should be given our rights,” he said. The ADC factional leader maintained that anyone seeking to join the party or contest elective positions on its platform must comply with its constitutional provisions, particularly those governing ward registration, membership dues and eligibility for leadership positions. According to him, the party’s constitution requires members to fulfil specified conditions, including two years of membership and payment of stipulated dues, before becoming eligible for leadership positions. He accused the opposing faction of disregarding the party’s registration procedures, alleging that Mark obtained his membership card from a former national chairman in Abuja rather than registering at his ward. Bala said he had repeatedly warned the opposing group about the consequences of failing to follow the party’s constitution but that his advice was ignored. On the continued appearance of Atiku’s and Mark’s names on INEC’s portal, he said the commission was law-abiding and would take appropriate action after receiving the Certified True Copy of the judgment. He dismissed suggestions that INEC was deliberately delaying the implementation of the judgment, explaining that the commission might not have received the official court document. Bala also rejected arguments that the large crowds attracted by the ADC during political engagements in Sokoto and Kebbi states should have persuaded him to withdraw his legal action. He argued that political popularity and financial influence should not be used to justify disregard for established laws, warning that the country could not make progress if influential politicians were allowed to operate outside constitutional provisions. He further alleged that some individuals involved in the dispute had circulated documents suggesting that he had resigned from his position, describing the claims as misleading. Speaking on his relationship with Atiku, Bala said he regarded the former vice-president as a father figure because they hailed from the same geopolitical zone. He, however, expressed disappointment that Atiku had not personally contacted him despite the controversy, while some party chieftains had continued to portray him as a spoiler. Bala said his faction had directed all aspirants seeking elective positions on the ADC platform to continue their campaign activities. He also urged members of the opposing faction to exercise patience, comply with the party’s constitutional provisions and complete their membership registration at their respective wards. On the party’s funding, he said his faction relied largely on membership dues and other contributions generated through its internal activities. He also defended his security arrangements and lifestyle, saying he was entitled to protection like other prominent political figures. He added that he was a businessman with other sources of livelihood. Bala urged Nigerian youths to remain law-abiding and avoid being drawn into political confrontations, stressing that opposition politics should be conducted with respect for democratic institutions and the rule of law. The post I went to court to defend my rights, not working for APC to destabilise opposition — Nafiu Bala appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Who Gets To Compete?
item.description: Opposition talks are continuing. Campaigns are gathering pace. But access, legal certainty and confidence in the vote are becoming defining questions of the election. In Yelwata, Peter Obi stood before a community carrying the wounds of mass violence. In Akure, the APC called its organisation to work for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election. In London, INEC’s chairman faced questions about whether Nigerians could trust the coming vote. These were different settings for the same election. Together, they reveal a contest in which persuading voters is only part of the task. Candidates must sustain their organisations, establish their right to participate and reach citizens safely. The electoral commission must demonstrate that those citizens’ choices will be recorded faithfully. The week’s developments sharpen a fundamental question: how open, credible and competitive will the road to 2027 remain? Lagos Raises the Stakes Thursday’s reported attack on an NDC town hall gathering in Oregun, Lagos, deserves particular attention. According to reporting from the scene, armed men disrupted the gathering, participants were injured and a suspect was arrested. The NDC alleged political responsibility; the Lagos APC denied sponsoring the incident. The report established no independent evidence linking the attackers to a political party. Investigation must establish who acted, who organised them and whether anyone provided support. The democratic principle requires no such delay: citizens must be able to attend lawful political meetings without fearing assault. Violence can influence an election before a ballot is cast. It can discourage attendance, make venues reluctant to host meetings, increase campaign costs and persuade volunteers to stay home. Its effects therefore extend beyond the immediate victims. When intimidation restricts participation, it changes the conditions under which candidates compete. Political leaders should condemn attacks consistently, including when the victims support their opponents. Security agencies must provide protection on the same basis. Makinde Keeps the Alliance Door Open Seyi Makinde’s latest comments give fresh substance to the opposition’s continuing conversation about cooperation. In an interview reported today, the Oyo governor confirmed active discussions involving Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi. He said decisions should draw on evidence, manifestos, previous performance and public sentiment. He did not announce an agreement or endorse a preferred candidate. That distinction separates a development worth watching from a coalition already formed. item.dc:creator: Donatus Anichukwueze
item.content:encoded: Opposition talks are continuing. Campaigns are gathering pace. But access, legal certainty and confidence in the vote are becoming defining questions of the election. In Yelwata, Peter Obi stood before a community carrying the wounds of mass violence. In Akure, the APC called its organisation to work for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election. In London, INEC’s chairman faced questions about whether Nigerians could trust the coming vote. These were different settings for the same election. Together, they reveal a contest in which persuading voters is only part of the task. Candidates must sustain their organisations, establish their right to participate and reach citizens safely. The electoral commission must demonstrate that those citizens’ choices will be recorded faithfully. The week’s developments sharpen a fundamental question: how open, credible and competitive will the road to 2027 remain? Lagos Raises the Stakes Thursday’s reported attack on an NDC town hall gathering in Oregun, Lagos, deserves particular attention. According to reporting from the scene, armed men disrupted the gathering, participants were injured and a suspect was arrested. The NDC alleged political responsibility; the Lagos APC denied sponsoring the incident. The report established no independent evidence linking the attackers to a political party. Investigation must establish who acted, who organised them and whether anyone provided support. The democratic principle requires no such delay: citizens must be able to attend lawful political meetings without fearing assault. Violence can influence an election before a ballot is cast. It can discourage attendance, make venues reluctant to host meetings, increase campaign costs and persuade volunteers to stay home. Its effects therefore extend beyond the immediate victims. When intimidation restricts participation, it changes the conditions under which candidates compete. Political leaders should condemn attacks consistently, including when the victims support their opponents. Security agencies must provide protection on the same basis. Makinde Keeps the Alliance Door Open Seyi Makinde’s latest comments give fresh substance to the opposition’s continuing conversation about cooperation. In an interview reported today, the Oyo governor confirmed active discussions involving Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi. He said decisions should draw on evidence, manifestos, previous performance and public sentiment. He did not announce an agreement or endorse a preferred candidate. That distinction separates a development worth watching from a coalition already formed. The negotiations face a familiar practical difficulty: cooperation requires choices that impose costs on participants. Someone may need to surrender an ambition, accept another candidate’s leadership or persuade supporters to work with former rivals. An agreement also needs to travel beyond the negotiating room. State organisations, constituency candidates, volunteers and polling agents must understand what has been decided and how it affects them. Makinde’s willingness to discuss cooperation keeps options alive. Its electoral significance will depend on whether the discussions produce commitments that participants can implement. For now, opposition unity remains a possibility under negotiation. Atiku’s Uncertainty Has an Administrative Cost The ADC’s legal dispute continues to affect the wider contest. Speaking at Chatham House on Thursday, INEC chairman Joash Amupitan said the commission would obey binding court decisions concerning Atiku’s participation. He also disclosed that INEC faces more than 300 pending cases and warned that unresolved disputes complicate election preparations. His remarks should not be presented as a new judgment removing Atiku from the race. They state INEC’s position on compliance with court orders. The ADC says it has appealed the November 5 ruling and applied for a stay of execution. The reporting reviewed for this edition does not establish that the stay has subsequently been granted. The political consequences of uncertainty are substantial. Candidates need to plan expenditure, organisers need direction and supporters need reliable information. INEC needs clarity for materials and logistics. The public deserves precise reporting through this process: what the court ordered, what has been challenged and what any subsequent order changes. Accusations, assurances and legal outcomes should remain clearly distinguished. Benue Brings the Campaign Back to Human Security Obi’s visit to Yelwata on Wednesday moved from an announced engagement to a completed one. He met people affected by the June 2025 attack and announced support for orphaned children’s education and a borehole. He also held a town hall in Makurdi with his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. The visit gave insecurity a human setting beyond campaign statistics. For affected communities, security means being able to farm, send children to school, travel and return home. Recovery also requires care for survivors and a sustainable livelihood. Every candidate seeking their votes should explain how those conditions would be restored. Obi’s pledges invite scrutiny of the proposed methods and resources. The government’s record invites scrutiny of protection, prevention and recovery already delivered. Citizens should be able to compare both. APC Organisation Faces a Turnout Test In Akure on Wednesday, Vice-President Kashim Shettima represented Tinubu at the APC presidential rally, urging unity and mobilisation while challenging the strength of Atiku’s and Obi’s political support. The campaign set a target of 1.2 million votes in Ondo. That is an aspiration, rather than a forecast. The APC’s argument rests partly on its ability to organise. Its opponents are being challenged to demonstrate comparable reach. But organisation earns its electoral value through persuasion and turnout. Endorsements and attendance help show that a campaign is active; they do not establish how the wider electorate will vote. The economic argument remains central. Tinubu must explain how continuity will improve daily life. His challengers must demonstrate that their alternatives are workable and that they possess the capacity to implement them. A Date to Circle: November 28 INEC has announced a nationwide mock accreditation exercise for November 28, intended to test accreditation and electronic result transmission. Amupitan says the commission has procured additional BVAS devices and reduced the maximum number of voters assigned to each machine from 1,250 to 850. These are announced preparations; their effectiveness remains to be tested. The exercise provides a concrete opportunity to assess readiness. The useful questions will concern performance: accreditation success, equipment failures, transmission delays, discrepancies and the response when something goes wrong. Publishing those findings and the resulting corrections would give citizens evidence with which to judge INEC’s assurances. The position at week’s end: • APC/Tinubu: continuing mobilisation, with the challenge of translating political organisation and the government’s record into votes. • ADC/Atiku: campaigning under legal uncertainty, making authoritative court decisions especially consequential. • NDC/Obi-Kwankwaso: maintaining public engagements while facing concerns about campaign safety and the task of building electoral organisation. • APM/Makinde: keeping cooperation discussions open, with no completed alliance established by the latest comments. No fresh, credible polling in the material reviewed supports declaring a national swing this week. Recent local and off-cycle elections remain useful indicators when assessed alongside turnout, competitiveness and local conditions. Their results cannot simply be transferred to a presidential contest. The Cost of Taking Part For younger Nigerians, the campaign presents t

item.title: 2027: Why Atiku could win presidential election
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s 2027 presidential ambition is drawing attention amid growing discontent with the All Progressives Congress, APC, in Northern Nigeria, claims of a shift in the late President Muhammadu Buhari’s political support base and mounting public frustration over economic hardship. Read Also: * 2027: Why Tinubu may still win presidential election * 2027: Why Peter Obi could win presidential election Although President Bola Tinubu retains the advantages of incumbency and an extensive political structure, developments in the North, where Atiku has considerable political networks, could provide the former vice-president with an opportunity to mount a formidable challenge in the next presidential election. The emerging political calculations are being driven by Atiku’s renewed mobilisation efforts, claims of a possible realignment of Buhari’s political followers and the growing expectation that economic dissatisfaction could become a major factor in the 2027 contest. Atiku has placed considerable emphasis on Northern voter mobilisation, urging supporters in Sokoto to mobilise their families, friends and communities, turn out massively and protect their ballots. “I appeal to every one of you to come out, mobilise your families, your friends and all well-wishers. Vote massively, protect your vote, and make sure your vote is counted and announced,” he said. He warned that poor turnout could undermine the opposition’s numerical strength. “If you fail to turn out in large numbers, people will go from village to village buying voters’ cards to create the impression that we do not have as many supporters as those in the South,” he warned. The former vice-president’s emphasis on turnout reflects the importance of translating political support into actual votes, particularly in a region whose electoral strength could prove decisive in the next presidential contest. Northern calculations Adding another dimension to Atiku’s Northern calculations, former Minister of Sports and Youth Development, Solomon Dalung, an African Democratic Congress, ADC, chieftain who served under Buhari, claimed that the late president’s political following was shifting towards Atiku. Dalung linked the development to a reported visit by Buhari’s widow, Aisha, to the former vice-president. He described it as evidence of a political realignment. “The message she took for any politician to know is that the 12 million votes have been successfully transferred. We have had a phone call from the grave of Buhari that we should vote Atiku,” he said. He also expressed confidence that Atiku could defeat Tinubu, arguing that the former vice-president remained a formidable political contender despite the challenges facing his platform. “I am confident that as events are unfolding, Tinubu, even if he would take over the ADC secretariat and stop ADC from campaigning, cannot defeat Atiku Abubakar in 2027,” Dalung said. Read Also: * 2027: Why Tinubu may still win presidential election * 2027: Why Peter Obi could win presidential election Although President Bola Tinubu retains the advantages of incumbency and an extensive political structure, developments in the North, where Atiku has considerable political networks, could provide the former vice-president with an opportunity to mount a formidable challenge in the next presidential election. The emerging political calculations are being driven by Atiku’s renewed mobilisation efforts, claims of a possible realignment of Buhari’s political followers and the growing expectation that economic dissatisfaction could become a major factor in the 2027 contest. Atiku has placed considerable emphasis on Northern voter mobilisation, urging supporters in Sokoto to mobilise their families, friends and communities, turn out massively and protect their ballots. “I appeal to every one of you to come out, mobilise your families, your friends and all well-wishers. Vote massively, protect your vote, and make sure your vote is counted and announced,” he said. He warned that poor turnout could undermine the opposition’s numerical strength. “If you fail to turn out in large numbers, people will go from village to village buying voters’ cards to create the impression that we do not have as many supporters as those in the South,” he warned. The former vice-president’s emphasis on turnout reflects the importance of translating political support into actual votes, particularly in a region whose electoral strength could prove decisive in the next presidential contest. Northern calculations Adding another dimension to Atiku’s Northern calculations, former Minister of Sports and Youth Development, Solomon Dalung, an African Democratic Congress, ADC, chieftain who served under Buhari, claimed that the late president’s political following was shifting towards Atiku. Dalung linked the development to a reported visit by Buhari’s widow, Aisha, to the former vice-president. He described it as evidence of a political realignment. “The message she took for any politician to know is that the 12 million votes have been successfully transferred. We have had a phone call from the grave of Buhari that we should vote Atiku,” he said. He also expressed confidence that Atiku could defeat Tinubu, arguing that the former vice-president remained a formidable political contender despite the challenges facing his platform. “I am confident that as events are unfolding, Tinubu, even if he would take over the ADC secretariat and stop ADC from campaigning, cannot defeat Atiku Abubakar in 2027,” Dalung said. Although Dalung’s claim about the transfer of Buhari’s 12 million votes is a partisan political assertion rather than a verified movement of voters, it highlights the importance Atiku’s supporters attach to the late president’s political legacy and its possible implications for the 2027 election. Economic realities Beyond the Northern political calculations, economic hardship could provide another opening for the opposition. Rising living costs, food insecurity, unemployment and persistent insecurity have intensified public concerns about the direction of the country under the Tinubu administration. For Atiku, the opportunity lies in converting those grievances into electoral support through a convincing alternative on economic management, security and job creation. However, his ambition faces significant obstacles. The APC retains the advantages of incumbency, serving governors and established grassroots structures, while Atiku must rebuild his appeal beyond his traditional Northern support base, particularly in the South. There is also the unresolved legal uncertainty surrounding the ADC leadership and the implications of the Federal High Court judgment for the party’s political activities and candidates. Ultimately, the 2027 contest could test whether dissatisfaction with the Tinubu administration, combined with Atiku’s Northern political networks and the possible realignment of Buhari’s supporters, can translate into a broader national electoral challenge. item.title: ‘Truly beautiful’ to make football return, says Ronaldinho
item.description: Brazilian great Ronaldinho says it will be “truly beautiful” to make his return to the pitch on Sunday, 11 years after retirement, when he plays for Italian third-tier side Ravenna. The 46-year-old, who last played for Fluminense in 2015, will start for Ravenna in their local derby against Forli. “I want to have a great day. I’m happy to be here for the start of this wonderful story,” Ronaldinho told Sky Sports on Friday. “The president dreams of something big for Ravenna, and being a part of it makes me happy.” Ravenna president Ignazio Cipriani has said his goal is to take the club to Serie A for the first time in their history. The team’s Stadio Bruno Benelli, which usually holds 5,000 fans, is sold out, with a 1,800-capacity temporary stand — dubbed “R10” — also erected for the occasion. Ravenna, who have not even played in Serie B since 2008, are second in their group in Serie C, six points behind leaders Spezia. “Returning to the pitch after so much time is truly beautiful — I’m here to experience a special moment in my life,” added Ronaldinho. “It’s been a few years since I stopped playing — I’ve won everything I ever dreamed of. “Now I’m 46, and I’ve experienced everything there is to experience in football. This is a completely different kind of opportunity. I want to be part of the dream held by my friends who work for Ravenna.” The 2005 Ballon d’Or winner will be hoping to score his 300th career goal, over a decade after he netted his 299th. The former Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain star has even spent time in a Paraguayan prison since, after attempting to enter the country on a false passport, but did star in a prison futsal match. The move to Ravenna is widely regarded as a marketing stunt, but one Cipriani hopes can help kickstart his Serie A dream. “The long-term goal is to get Ravenna promoted to Serie A,” insisted the club president. The post ‘Truly beautiful’ to make football return, says Ronaldinho appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: I received N100m alert after APC campaign – Portable
item.description: Nigerian singer, Habeeb Okikiola, popularly known as Portable, has claimed that Ogun State All Progressive Congress governorship candidate, Senator Solomon Adeola, also known as Yayi, sent him N100m after he participated in campaign activities for the party. Portable made the claim in a video circulating on social media on Friday, where he expressed excitement over the alleged payment and thanked Adeola and another politician, IBD Dende. In the footage, the singer wore an APC-branded shirt and a cap bearing Yayi’s name, while displaying campaign materials featuring the senator. He explained that IBD Dende had earlier asked him to return home and promised to contact him, but some of his associates later informed him that the senator was looking for him. The singer said he initially doubted the information because of an earlier experience in which he was reportedly told that money had been sent to him, but he received nothing. “My dearest fans! I just woke up to an alert of N100m from Yayi! IBD Dende, oga mi! God bless you. Thank you! Yayi instructed them to send me the money. I took a nap, and God saved me from death,” he said. Portable added that he was initially suspicious when he heard that Adeola wanted to reach him. “Are you the one to tell me that Yayi is looking for me?’ I asked. They wanted to scam me, just as they did when Yayi sent money previously. I did not get a dime then,” he said. “Thank you, Lord! Yayi has sent N100m. Thank you, IBD Dende. May your children be glorious! May you live long, my daddy. It shall be well with you. N100m is not a small amount at all!” he added. The claim comes weeks after Portable publicly acknowledged receiving payments for taking part in APC campaign activities in support of President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general elections. The post I received N100m alert after APC campaign – Portable appeared first on Vanguard News .
